items.summary: On October 14, 2026, eight state attorneys general filed coordinated lawsuits against OpenAI, alleging illegal activities including unfounded safety claims and improper data collection from children. These suits, filed in various state courts, echo previous claims against Meta regarding deceptive practices and privacy violations. Simultaneously, private litigation organizations filed additional suits in California on behalf of individuals harmed by the AI products, including a case involving a poisoning plot and another concerning a teenager's suicide. A separate class action lawsuit accuses OpenAI of unlawful business practices targeting minors. OpenAI responded by stating it has built industry-leading age-specific protections and is committed to advancing pragmatic AI policies. The article notes that the jury is still out on whether these legal actions will mark a turning point for AI regulation similar to the "Big Tobacco moment" for social media.
items.title: Multiple Lawsuits Target OpenAI Over Safety and Data Practices

items.summary: The Sanatan Raksha Sangathan reportedly placed posters in Lucknow depicting Indian and international figures as a ten-headed Ravana ahead of Dussehra. The posters, titled 'Sanatan Bharat Ke Virodhi Ravan,' feature leaders like Rahul Gandhi and Elon Musk, accusing them of opposing India's interests. The organization used the festival's symbolism to create a political narrative against these personalities.
items.title: Sanatan Raksha Sangathan Posts Anti-India Ravana Posters in Lucknow

items.summary: The combined market valuation of nine top Indian firms surged by ₹3.65 lakh crore last week, with TCS leading gains. The rally followed a strong week for the BSE Sensex and NSE Nifty, driven by rebounding IT stocks and renewed buying interest in heavyweight companies. TCS emerged as the biggest gainer, while Larsen & Toubro was the only laggard among the ten firms.
items.title: Nine Top Indian Firms See Market Cap Surge Led by TCS

items.summary: Nine of India's 10 most valuable companies added approximately Rs 3.65 lakh crore to their market capitalisation last week, supported by a strong stock market recovery. Tata Consultancy Services led the rally with a gain of Rs 1.08 lakh crore, while Larsen & Toubro was the only firm to lose value. The rally was driven by strong buying in IT and banking stocks following encouraging September quarter earnings.
items.title: Nine Top Indian Firms Added 3.65 Lakh Crore in Market Value Last Week

items.summary: Stores of major brands including Celine, Dior, Hermès and Apple were looted and vandalised across several French cities on Saturday. The unrest occurred as nationwide protests over rising living costs and deteriorating public services turned violent. The Galeries Lafayette department store in Paris was also targeted, while supermarkets, pharmacies, electronics stores and other businesses were raided in cities including Marseille, Nice, Nantes, Bordeaux, Lille, Toulouse and Strasbourg.
items.title: Major French Retailers Looted During Nationwide Violent Protests

items.summary: Google cofounder Sergey Brin donated over $100 million to oppose California's Proposition 40, a billionaire wealth tax. However, he will not vote on the measure next month after changing his residency to Nevada. Brin, whose net worth is estimated at $263 billion, purchased a $42 million mansion in Nevada. The tax would apply to California residents starting January 1, 2026.
items.title: Sergey Brin Donates Against California Wealth Tax While Avoiding Vote

items.summary: With approximately 30 days remaining until the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, China is intensifying preparations. The city is launching a 'Green Travel, Smooth Journey for All' plan, adding over 50 new bus-metro feeder routes and increasing bus services by 20%. Officials are calling for stronger coordination across security, healthcare, and logistics to ensure smooth operations for world leaders meeting in mid-November 2026.
items.title: Shenzhen Prepares for APEC 2026 with Enhanced Transport and Security Measures

items.summary: MIT researchers have developed a multimodal AI model to address limitations in using large language models for materials discovery. The new system combines 3D atomic structures with natural language descriptions, allowing the AI to 'see' atomic arrangements and bonding patterns. In a study published in Nature Communications, the team demonstrated that their model could identify promising material designs for applications like solid-state lithium-ion battery electrolytes more effectively than text-only models. Ju Li, a professor at MIT, noted that understanding structure is foundational to inferring material properties. The research, supported by agencies including the U.S. Defense Threat Reduction Agency, aims to accelerate materials science by bridging the gap between atomic structure and functional properties.
items.title: MIT Researchers Develop Multimodal AI for Materials Discovery

items.summary: 7-Eleven is introducing hot-food counters at 16 Singapore outlets as part of DFI Retail Group's growth strategy. The new Foodbar concept offers customisable bowls and snacks like pizza and waffles. This expansion follows a survey showing rising demand for ready-to-eat meals. DFI also plans to broaden food offerings at Starbucks and Guardian stores.
items.title: 7-Eleven Expands Hot-Food Counters in Singapore Stores

items.summary: According to Taiwan's tourism department, residents made over 2.49 million trips to the Chinese mainland in the first eight months of 2026, a 19.63% increase. Monthly visits exceeded 300,000 from March through August. While overall outbound travel grew 15.24%, mainland trips expanded faster. Travel preferences vary by generation, with older travelers favoring group tours to scenic regions and younger people preferring independent trips to cities like Shanghai and Chongqing, often inspired by social media.
items.title: Taiwan Residents Increase Mainland Travel by Nearly 20% in 2026

items.summary: The article examines China's aging demographic, noting a senior population exceeding 320 million, including 35 million functionally impaired elders. It highlights the nation's efforts to address this shift through grassroots long-term care schemes and emerging eldercare technologies. The piece features human stories and innovations aimed at redefining aging well for the country's 1.4 billion people.
items.title: China Quest Explores Aging Population Challenges and Innovations

items.summary: The Ministry of Commerce proposed adding photovoltaic technologies to China's export-control list, citing their use in sensitive areas like aerospace and national defense. Officials held initial talks with manufacturers about potential curbs on advanced solar-panel manufacturing technologies. Beijing has also restricted exports of solar-manufacturing technology to India. Analysts suggest China aims to preserve its dominance as India builds domestic manufacturing capabilities.
items.title: China Proposes Export Controls on Solar Technologies for National Security

items.summary: Vietnam signed a free trade agreement with the European Free Trade Association on October 18 in Hanoi. The deal eliminates or reduces customs duties on industrial, fish, and agricultural products. Officials stated the agreement aims to reinforce the rules-based trading system and diversify markets amid US tariff disruptions. Bilateral trade last year was valued at 4.8 billion euros.
items.title: Vietnam Signs Free Trade Deal With Four European Nations

items.summary: NVIDIA has launched RTX Spark laptops featuring Blackwell RTX graphics and up to 128GB of unified memory. Starting at $2,399, these devices from partners like ASUS and Dell bring local AI and gaming capabilities to Windows PCs. NVIDIA celebrated the global launch with events in cities including Berlin, Beijing, and Seoul, where CEO Jensen Huang made a surprise appearance.
items.title: NVIDIA Launches RTX Spark Laptops with Blackwell RTX Graphics

items.summary: Yokohama's upcoming Green Expo aims to highlight environmental sustainability by reviving Edo Period practices like circularity and disaster mitigation. Organizers plan to plant ten million plants and reuse timber from the Osaka Expo to symbolize a zero-waste society while addressing modern climate challenges.
items.title: Yokohama Green Expo Draws on Edo Period Sustainability

items.summary: Condé Nast's UK profits fell 36% to nearly £18m last year, driven by higher restructuring costs and lower UK revenues, though international growth kept total revenue flat. The Newhouse family ruled out a sale despite speculation from Jeff Bezos, citing a century-long commitment to media ownership. Staff numbers remained stable despite cost increases.
items.title: Condé Nast UK Profits Drop as Sale Ruled Out

items.summary: Analysis indicates the quality-adjusted screen time price index has decreased by 39 per cent since 2000. This decline is primarily attributed to improvements in device quality rather than lower prices. Consequently, real-terms spending per person on digital technology has risen by 52 per cent over the past 20 years. The shift reflects digital technology's dominance through convenience and attention capture, despite mounting financial and social costs.
items.title: Screen Time Price Index Falls Due to Quality Gains

items.summary: Heating oil prices have risen by up to 82% since the start of the US-Israeli war with Iran, according to the Minister for Energy Consumers. Residents in the South West report holding off on fuel purchases, fearing they may go without. The government announced new measures to regulate the market and review minimum order levels, though some customers remain skeptical about their ability to lower costs.
items.title: Heating Oil Prices Soar Amid Conflict; Customers Face Winter Hardship

items.summary: Research by E3G suggests that insulating homes and investing in heat pumps would reduce living costs and boost the UK economy more effectively than drilling for new oil. The government's warm homes plan could slash £1bn annually from household bills and provide a £1.6bn yearly economic boost, creating 50,000 jobs. In contrast, the Rosebank oilfield is projected to create only 1,100 jobs. While proponents argue oil developments support economic value, experts note that tax revenues are limited by concessions and that decommissioning costs could outweigh benefits. The study highlights that new oil and gas would not lower fuel prices due to international market dynamics.
items.title: Study Finds Home Insulation Beats Oil Drilling for UK Economy

items.summary: Oil prices remain elevated as the conflict between the U.S., Israel, and Iran extends into 2027, tightening global supply. ICE Brent crude futures for January 2027 trade at $102.59 per barrel, significantly higher than December 2025 levels of less than $70. The International Energy Agency plans to release over 20 million barrels of diesel, potentially reaching 50 million barrels, to address the shortage. Despite reports of recovering oil flows, trust in official figures is low, and refining capacity remains short. The IMF projects global economic growth of 3.4% next year, but central bankers warn that resilience is reaching its limits due to high energy costs.
items.title: Oil Prices Remain High Amid Prolonged Middle East Conflict

items.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio is scheduled to meet Reliance Industries chairman Mukesh Ambani in Jamnagar, Gujarat. The visit, part of a broader trip to India, coincides with Reliance Industries' preparations for an investment in a Texas oil refinery. Reports indicate the meeting aims to deepen bilateral energy cooperation, though official confirmation is pending.
items.title: US Secretary Rubio to Meet Reliance Chairman Ambani in Jamnagar Amid Texas Refinery Plans

items.summary: Violent protests against rising living costs in France escalated to widespread looting and arson across cities like Paris, Marseille, and Lille. Authorities reported 1,200 arrests and 150 injured officers. While the interior ministry estimated 550,000 participants, the CGT union cited 800,000. Prime Minister Lecornu confirmed the arrests, and President Macron vowed prosecution for vandalism and looting.
items.title: French Protests Escalate to Looting and Violence Across Major Cities

items.summary: Singapore palm oil stocks fell as the government investigated firms linked to haze-causing fires in Indonesia. Wilmar International, Golden Agri Resources, Bumitama Agri, and First Resources addressed queries, denying responsibility or citing external causes. Meanwhile, Deluge launched on the SGX, and tech stocks recovered after a global rout. SGX reported resilient performance with rising turnover and record inflows into STI ETFs. The Straits Times Index reached a record high, driven by retail investor inflows.
items.title: Singapore Palm Oil Stocks Tumble Amid Haze Investigation

items.summary: The 140th Canton Fair in Guangzhou, China's Guangdong Province, highlights digitalization, smart technology, and green development as its central themes. Visitors can explore the latest high-tech innovations, including AI-powered products and robots, on display at the event. Attendees are also informed about cookie usage and privacy policies through the website.
items.title: Canton Fair Showcases Digitalization and Smart Technology in Guangzhou

items.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy suggested a potential trilateral meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin could occur in the United States during the upcoming G20 Summit in December, pending confirmation from Moscow and Washington. Zelenskyy emphasized the need for increased pressure on Moscow and expressed readiness to negotiate in any format. Meanwhile, Zelenskyy criticized US President Donald Trump for waiving additional tariffs on Russian oil under the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, stating the move fuels Russian satisfaction and does not stop the war. Trump claimed both leaders want the conflict to end.
items.title: Zelenskyy Hints at Trilateral Meeting with Putin in US Amid Tariff Waiver

items.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio is visiting India to discuss stalled trade negotiations, bypassing the capital to focus on investment and energy. Experts attribute the delay to legal uncertainty surrounding US tariffs and India's reluctance to expose farmers to competition. While trade volumes have risen, officials describe progress as having hit a plateau with little room for further concessions.
items.title: US-India Trade Deal Stalled Amid Tariff Uncertainty and Negotiation Hurdles

items.summary: US President Donald Trump waived provisions of the Lindsey Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act, removing a threat of 100% tariffs on Russian oil buyers. While this offers relief to India, experts caution the move is not India-specific and remains reversible. The waiver coincides with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio's visit to India amid declining Indian imports of American energy.
items.title: Trump Waives Tariffs on Russian Oil Buyers, India Benefits

items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi expressed grief over the deaths of 14 people after a truck crashed into devotees in Gwalior. He announced Rs 2 lakh relief for the next of kin of each deceased. Additionally, he provided Rs 50,000 financial assistance from the PMNRF for each of the nearly 40 injured persons.
items.title: PM Modi Announces Relief for Gwalior Accident Victims

items.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio explained that the United States waived potential 100% tariffs on India and four other nations purchasing Russian oil and gas. Rubio stated that while India has diversified its energy imports, it is difficult to pivot away from Russian supplies in a single day. President Donald Trump invoked a waiver clause under the Lindsey O Graham Act, deferring secondary sanctions to analyze the global economic impact. This decision follows a new US diesel supply deal with Moscow, involving millions of tons of fuel. The move is seen as a conciliatory step ahead of the November 3 midterm elections.
items.title: US Waives Russia Energy Tariffs for India Amid Pivot Challenges

items.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio clarified that a waiver on sanctions and tariffs against Russian energy imports is a temporary 60-day measure. Signed by President Trump, it allows the administration to assess global economic impacts before deciding on further action. The waiver addresses India's reliance on Russian oil while evaluating the complexities of secondary sanctions on key US allies amid volatile energy markets.
items.title: Rubio Clarifies Temporary US Waiver on Russia Energy Tariffs for India

items.summary: Deferred 100% US tariffs provide only temporary relief to India as Russian oil imports decline. Indian refiners reduced exposure before the Lindsey O Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act became law, anticipating enforcement difficulties. Imports of discounted Russian crude fell by a third since July, while India's crude import bill rose 31.6% in September. Experts note the waiver offers no long-term assurance for energy security or trade talks, leaving Washington free to revive tariff threats. Ajay Srivastava stated the waiver buys time but offers no lasting certainty.
items.title: Deferred US Tariffs Offer Temporary Relief as India Cuts Russian Oil

items.summary: Actress Neha Sharma issued an official warning via her X account against the unauthorized creation and sharing of AI-generated images and videos featuring her likeness. She expressed concern that such manipulated content could misrepresent her identity and harm her reputation. Sharma demanded the immediate removal of existing material and urged users to stop creating new content without permission, stating she would pursue legal action against violators.
items.title: Neha Sharma Warns Against Unauthorized AI Use of Her Likeness

items.summary: Telangana BJP President N Ramchander Rao termed the Kolkata Durga Puja stampede, which claimed 19 lives and injured 25 others, a major tragedy. Rao called for a thorough probe to fix responsibility and take action against those responsible. He expressed confidence that the West Bengal government would conduct an investigation and hold the accountable parties liable. Meanwhile, Kolkata Police arrested seven individuals, including puja committee officials and security personnel, and registered a suo motu case. The West Bengal government announced compensation of Rs 25 lakh and a job for each deceased person's family. Rao also criticized opposition leaders for remarks on regime change, drawing parallels to Bangladesh.
items.title: Telangana BJP Chief Calls for Probe After Kolkata Stampede

items.summary: Australia and South Africa are set for their second Test match in Gqeberha, following Australia's victory in Durban. South Africa made squad changes, including the return of Kagiso Rabada and the promotion of Matthew Breetzke, while Australia aims to secure the series.
items.title: Australia and South Africa prepare for second Test in Gqeberha

items.summary: A large fire near Canadian Forces Base Wainwright in Alberta has killed or injured several people, according to the nation's defence minister. The incident occurred during a live-fire training exercise, possibly involving a gas line. Authorities describe the situation as active and delicate, with emergency services managing the response while neighboring provinces offer support.
items.title: Major Fire at Canadian Military Base Leaves Several Dead or Injured

items.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and Defence Minister David McGuinty announced a serious incident at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright involving a major fire. The officials confirmed fatalities and injuries but stated that further details would be released in the coming hours and days. McGuinty expressed sadness and noted that thoughts were with the affected personnel.
items.title: Canadian officials report fatalities and injuries at military base fire

items.summary: A stampede at a Durga Puja pandal in Kolkata killed 19 people after heavy rainfall caused overcrowding and panic. Poor crowd management and narrow exits contributed to the tragedy. Police arrested seven individuals, including committee officials, for negligence. The Centre and state government announced financial compensation for the deceased and injured. Senior officials visited the injured and ordered investigations.
items.title: Stampede at Kolkata Durga Puja Pandal Kills 19

items.summary: Aditya Chakrabortty presents a review of Michael Gove's political trajectory, suggesting further reading on his past writings and current standing. The episode features recommendations from historians and political analysts regarding the Conservative Party's evolution, Brexit's economic impact, and contemporary political discourse. Listeners are directed to specific essays, books, and columns for deeper insight into these topics.
items.title: Aditya Chakrabortty reviews Michael Gove's political career and related reading

items.summary: Firefighters rescued a teenager from a stormwater drain in Brisbane's Kangaroo Point area on Sunday afternoon. Emergency crews located the boy approximately 20 metres from the entrance using an inflatable rescue boat. The teenager was uninjured and did not require hospital treatment. Queensland Fire Department officer Clint Pilon described the operation as smooth and warned against playing in drains after rain.
items.title: Teenager Rescued from Brisbane Stormwater Drain After Getting Stuck

items.summary: As Durga Puja approaches, bhoger khichuri has emerged as a central symbol of the festival in Bengal, embodying the egalitarian spirit of sarbojonin Durga Puja. Made with Gobindobhog rice, roasted moong dal, and seasonal vegetables, this humble dish is prepared with care as an offering to the goddess before being shared communally. Hospitality entrepreneur Samrat Banerjee notes that khichuri holds a special place in Bengal's celebrations, while food historian Tanushree Bhowmik explains that the quality of ingredients and the reverence with which the dish is prepared and consumed make it sacred. The meal, often served on Ashtami, brings together devotees, volunteers, and visitors in a shared experience of nostalgia, community, and devotion, transcending social hierarchies and becoming a powerful moment of belonging.
items.title: How a simple plate of khichuri became a symbol of Bengal's Durga Puja

items.summary: Police in Greater Noida arrested three people suspected of involvement in the deaths of a couple and their three children. While initial signs suggested food poisoning from noodles, post-mortem reports indicated poisoning. Authorities suspect suicide but are investigating a property dispute and a voice note left by the deceased. The exact cause of death remains pending laboratory results.
items.title: Police Arrest Three in Greater Noida Family Deaths Probe

items.summary: A dispute over smart meter installation in Himachal Pradesh intensified after the electricity board cut power to Vinay Kumar Sharma, a panchayat pradhan in Bilaspur district, who refused to install one. Sharma threatened to remove poles on his land and filed a petition in the High Court. The board stated that disconnection follows a 24-hour notice under existing policy, while residents fear hardship from the meters.
items.title: Himachal Pradesh Smart Meter Dispute Escalates Over Power Cut

items.summary: The bilateral U.S.-Japan Keen Sword 27 military exercises are set to begin Monday, marking several firsts. These biannual drills, involving approximately 45,000 Self-Defense Force personnel and 12,000 U.S. service members, will see Japan deploy Type 25 surface-to-ship missiles outside Kumamoto Prefecture for the first time. Additionally, the U.S. side is sending an advanced anti-ship missile system to Yonaguni, an island in Okinawa Prefecture located 110 kilometers from Taiwan.
items.title: Joint Japan-U.S. Military Drill Set to Break New Ground

items.summary: Surajit C. Mukhopadhyay, a sociologist, argues that Durga Puja in Bengal uniquely merges religious devotion with secular public life. He notes that while the festival is a Hindu observance, its appeal extends beyond faith through artistic pandals, community gatherings, and entertainment. Mukhopadhyay explains that the event transforms urban spaces, allowing people to escape daily pressures while engaging with social issues. He traces the festival's evolution from private household worship to public community celebrations, highlighting how it accommodates diverse social groups despite persistent inequalities. The author concludes that Durga Puja serves as a vital cultural expression where tradition and modernity coexist, offering a shared public experience that cannot be reduced to mere ritual or commercial spectacle.
items.title: Sociologist Explains How Durga Puja Blends Sacred Rituals With Secular Public Celebration

items.summary: The Central Reserve Police Force is reportedly considering reintroducing the ranks of lance naik and naik, abolished in 1997, to address delayed promotions and boost morale. With constables waiting an average of 22–25 years for their first promotion, officials aim to create additional opportunities. The proposal remains under consideration pending feedback from field formations.
items.title: CRPF Considers Restoring Abolished Military Ranks to Address Promotion Delays

items.summary: Violent protests across France on Saturday turned destructive, with masked demonstrators setting fire to the 140-year-old Limoges town hall. Authorities state roughly 550,000 people participated nationwide. The prefecture reports rioters entered the building at 6 pm, causing its destruction. President Macron condemned the violence, stating those who vandalized public property will be prosecuted.
items.title: Violent Protests in France Destroy Historic Limoges Town Hall

items.summary: Months-long wildfires in Indonesia have generated severe toxic haze across Southeast Asia, prompting the highest-level alert from the ASEAN Specialised Meteorological Centre. Drought conditions linked to a severe 'super-El Nino' effect have exacerbated the fires, particularly on Borneo and Sumatra. The pollution has closed schools, restricted outdoor activities, and caused a surge in respiratory conditions in Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, and East Timor. While environmental groups report burned areas ranging from 637,000 to nearly 900,000 hectares, authorities in Indonesia attempted to disperse the haze using 2.4 tonnes of dry ice at a South Sumatra airport. Residents describe the situation as worsening their health and economic livelihoods.
items.title: Months-long Indonesia wildfires spew toxic haze across Southeast Asia

items.summary: Violent clashes, looting, and arson occurred across France during demonstrations against school hardship and the cost of living. Over 1,200 people were arrested, with an estimated 550,000 taking to the streets. Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu stated that 150 police officers were injured. In Saint-Étienne, Mayor Régis Juanico reported a young man had his hand blown off by an explosive. While some marches were peaceful, others involved fires and vehicle torching. Jean-Luc Mélenchon accused police of unleashing violence, while Emmanuel Macron promised prosecution for those who looted. The government offered 3,000 extra supply teachers, but protests intensified.
items.title: Violent Clashes and Looting Erupt Across France During Student Protests

items.summary: Police arrested seven people, including organizers, after a stampede at the Chorbagan Durga Puja pandal in Kolkata killed 19 people and injured dozens. The incident occurred on Saptami, the seventh day of the festival. West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari stated that an announcement by organizers triggered a rush, though it remains unclear what was announced. Secretary Raj Kumar Sewda was among those detained.
items.title: Seven Arrested After Durga Puja Stampede Kills 19 in Kolkata

items.summary: Chinese workers are training robots by performing everyday tasks like folding clothes and sweeping floors. Participants, including Liu Yun and Sun, wear sensors to record movements for machine learning. Earnings range from 120 to 135 yuan per shift, with some earning around 4,000 yuan monthly. While some find the work tiring, others value the flexibility. Critics compare it to a cyber assembly line, noting the irony of humans teaching machines that may eventually replace them.
items.title: Chinese Workers Train Robots for Household Chores

items.summary: Abhijeet Dipke, founder of India's youth-led Cockroach Janta Party, was released from police custody on Saturday following his detention for participating in a rally calling for the resignation of India's chief election commissioner. While Dipke was freed, two other CJP leaders remain detained after demonstrating at a prohibited protest site. The commission denies wrongdoing regarding allegations of voter roll manipulation, which activists claim benefit the ruling party.
items.title: India's Cockroach Movement Founder Released After Election Protest Arrest

items.summary: A bulldozer sent to remove a Communist Party of India (Marxist) book stall in Jadavpur, Kolkata, retreated after workers, residents, and students gathered to oppose the move. The incident occurred during Durga Puja, amidst disputes over Left parties' stalls. CPI(M) leader Sudip Sengupta stated they had necessary permissions, while authorities disputed some stalls' compliance. The action followed similar demolitions in Dhakuria and court interventions regarding stall locations.
items.title: Left Parties Force Bulldozer to Retreat from CPI(M) Stall in Jadavpur

items.summary: A Sunday briefing covered several international developments. The Saudi-led coalition reported intercepting two Houthi ballistic missiles targeting southwestern Saudi Arabia. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio expressed deep concern over an attack on American photojournalist Heidi Levine in the occupied West Bank, urging Israel to curb violence. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth warned Iran faces a choice between abandoning nuclear ambitions or facing devastating military action. The briefing also noted football match results and an art installation in London, alongside Meta's denial of political bias regarding Brazilian candidates and updates on its AI terms.
items.title: US Officials Address Regional Conflicts and Iran Nuclear Threat

items.summary: Conservation agencies in West Kalimantan and Indonesia rescued 51 orangutans from wildfires between August 6 and October 19. Officials noted the number could reach 96. The fires caused severe haze affecting air quality and travel across Southeast Asia, prompting flight cancellations and health alerts.
items.title: Conservation groups rescue dozens of orangutans from Indonesian wildfires

items.summary: Emergent Ventures has funded several archaeological initiatives. Björn Öste is developing Arkhub, an AI platform analyzing remote-sensing data to identify ancient sites in the Amazon for citizen scientists. Cameron Monroe leads a project in Benin using lidar and fieldwork to reconstruct the Kingdom of Allada. Other grantees include Benjamin Arbuckle, Jesse Casana, Leila Character, and Bryce Hoenigman, who are applying DNA analysis, radar imaging, drone tools, and AI to date cuneiform tablets, respectively. The organization notes remaining funds in this tranche.
items.title: Emergent Ventures Funds Archaeology Projects Using AI and Remote Sensing

items.summary: The Saudi-led coalition reported that two officers were killed when a Saudi National Guard reconnaissance helicopter crashed in the Najran region. Coalition spokesman Turki al-Maliki stated the AH-6i helicopter crashed inside Saudi territory due to a technical malfunction. He expressed condolences to the families of the deceased officers.
items.title: Saudi-led coalition reports two officers killed in helicopter crash in Najran

items.summary: Architect Adam Nathaniel Furman argues that the dominance of white in modern architecture stems from historical prejudice rather than aesthetic necessity. He cites an AI-generated image of a pink Guggenheim to illustrate that Frank Lloyd Wright originally envisioned the building in color. Furman's book, Chromatic Architecture, traces how the myth of a colorless classical world was cemented by scholars like Johann Joachim Winckelmann and later architects. Despite evidence of vibrant ancient structures and colorful modern alternatives, Furman contends that deep-seated assumptions continue to exclude color from contemporary design.
items.title: Architect Adam Nathaniel Furman Debunks White Modernism Myths

items.summary: A second energy crisis, triggered by wars in Ukraine and the Middle East, is dismantling resistance to a global shift away from fossil fuels. High gasoline and diesel prices in Europe have delivered a final blow to arguments against rapid electrification. Renewable installations set a new record last year, rising 15.5% worldwide, while electric car sales have surged in European markets. Industry leaders and analysts note that electrification will significantly reduce fossil fuel demand, with some predicting a structural shift toward alternative transportation. However, experts warn that electrifying alone is not enough; the electricity must be generated from clean sources to constitute a true transition.
items.title: Energy Crisis Accelerates Global Shift to Electric Power

items.summary: Paris police reported detaining a record 855 people during demonstrations in the capital. Clashes injured 13 officers and gendarmes. Nationwide protests, estimated at 800,000 participants, targeted austerity and living costs. Looters raided shops across France. A protester suffered a hand injury from a crowd-control grenade.
items.title: Police Detain Record Number of People During French Protests

items.summary: An out-of-control truck carrying paddy crashed into devotees near the Sheetla Mata Temple in Gwalior, killing 12 people and injuring 39. The vehicle broke through a police checkpoint on a restricted slope late Saturday night. Authorities are investigating how the truck bypassed security measures and have sent a team to inspect the vehicle mechanically.
items.title: Truck Crash Kills 12 and Injures 39 Near Gwalior Temple

items.summary: A newsletter highlights two distinct stories. First, hackers targeted refrigeration systems in French supermarkets, causing temperatures to reach 50°C and spoiling food. This incident underscores the risks of connecting industrial equipment to the internet. Second, Singapore's GovTech launched FirstDate, a dating app for public officers aged 21 to 35. The app utilizes the Gale-Shapley algorithm, originally developed in 1962 and associated with a 2012 Nobel Prize in Economics, to suggest single matches. By limiting choices, the app aims to encourage considered decisions in a country facing a low birth rate of 0.87 per woman in 2025. The piece also features reader recommendations for music and books.
items.title: Singapore Uses Nobel Algorithm for Dating App Amidst Cybersecurity Concerns

items.summary: A crackdown on sports piracy is intensifying as illegal streaming becomes endemic in British sports. Recent convictions include a man jailed for running an illegal service generating nearly £1m in profits and a postman sentenced for supplying pirate software to nearly 2,000 people. The industry faces significant pressure as advertising revenues fall and viewers shift away from long-term subscriptions. Research indicates that over 70% of 18 to 34-year-olds admit to using alternative means to watch paywalled content. While broadcasters previously viewed copyright theft as a manageable cost, the current economic climate has made it a serious concern. Illegal streaming costs the broadcasting industry approximately £700m annually. The practice is particularly prevalent among younger, digital-native audiences, though older viewers also participate. High costs and the 'blackout' policy driving fans to pirate streams are key factors. If left unchecked, piracy could hamper future growth and reduce revenues for sports rights holders.
items.title: Sports Piracy Threatens Broadcasting Revenue Models

items.summary: Residents of three Illinois towns successfully opposed a developer's plan to rezone rural land for a data center. Despite assurances that the project would proceed regardless of local opposition, community members gathered at town halls to voice their concerns. Their collective action led the developer, Karis Critical, to drop the proposal in late June. Amanda Pollard, a local resident, noted that the outcome demonstrates the community's ability to influence decisions. The initiative highlights the effectiveness of grassroots organizing in halting large-scale development projects.
items.title: Residents Successfully Stopped Data Center Plan in Illinois

items.summary: An assessment by the Secretariat of the Convention on Biological Diversity reports that nearly 90% of countries have established national biodiversity targets under the 2022 Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework. However, fewer than half of the assessed targets are on track for 2030. While protected areas are expanding and ecosystem restoration is advancing, progress on harmful subsidies and biodiversity finance remains slow. The findings highlight a significant gap between national commitments and the overall goals set to halt biodiversity loss by 2030, with a global review of progress scheduled for COP17 in Yerevan, Armenia.
items.title: Most Nations Set Biodiversity Goals but Lag on 2030 Targets

items.summary: David Fickling for Bloomberg Opinion reports that cash-strapped nations are increasingly relying on the International Islamic Trade Finance Corp (ITFC) to fund petroleum imports. While the ITFC has disbursed US$78 billion since 2008, primarily for semi-commercial lending to help countries pay for fuel, critics argue this approach defers underlying capital shortages and encourages reliance on fossil fuels. The commentary notes that between 2020 and 2024, total disbursements reached US$29 billion. It suggests that conventional development banks have been too slow to finance clean power, urging them to step up to avoid the energy transition being outspent by the fossil fuel economy.
items.title: Commentary on ITFC Financing Fossil Fuel Imports for Cash-Strapped Nations

items.summary: Anthropic is circulating a draft bill among US lawmakers to regulate artificial intelligence, addressing the lack of federal legislation. The proposal would allow the government to block models posing significant risks, requiring developers to test and evaluate powerful models. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei previously called for slowing development due to fears of AI agents taking control of the internet. The bill aims to override certain state laws and establish a robust security framework.
items.title: Anthropic Proposes AI Regulation Bill to US Lawmakers

items.summary: Tesla has unveiled a Roadster capable of launching itself into the air, marking a shift from science fiction to reality. Meanwhile, California startup Alef Aeronautics is developing its own flying car using different technology. CGTN’s Martin Markovits reports on this growing race to take transportation off the ground from Los Angeles.
items.title: Tesla and Alef Aeronautics Enter Electric Flying Car Race

items.summary: DeepSeek released the V4.1-Flash-1017 AI model, claiming stronger benchmark performance and faster task completion compared to its predecessor. The update aims to challenge US rivals like Anthropic and OpenAI. The firm cited improvements in reasoning and coding capabilities. Recent service disruptions and aggressive pricing have intensified competition in the open-weight model sector.
items.title: DeepSeek Unveils Faster AI Model Amid Intensifying Competition

items.summary: Anthropic has presented a draft bill to US lawmakers outlining regulations for artificial intelligence safety. The proposal suggests the government could block AI models that imminently risk killing or injuring more than 50 people or causing more than $1 billion in damages. These thresholds apply if the threat stems from a biological weapon, loss of control, or a cyberattack. The company advocates for mandatory testing and independent model reviews.
items.title: Anthropic Proposes AI Safety Bill to US Lawmakers

items.summary: Microsoft has terminated its agreement for a data center in Loughton, Essex, with British cloud provider Nscale, according to a report by Britain's Telegraph. The newspaper did not specify the reason for the withdrawal, though it noted Nscale faced repeated delays. National power grid officials reportedly told Nscale they do not expect power supply until the 2030s. An Nscale spokesperson stated the grid issue has no impact on other contracts and that the company remains committed to the project while exploring alternative power sources.
items.title: Microsoft Terminates UK Data Center Deal With Nscale Over Grid Delays

items.summary: Union minister Kiren Rijiju alleged on Sunday that opposition figures and politicians conspired to incite violence during anti-SIR protests in New Delhi, drawing parallels to unrest in Bangladesh and France. He stated India is neither Bangladesh nor France. Meanwhile, senior advocate Prashant Bhushan rejected the characterization of the agitation as an opposition-led regime change attempt, asserting that regime change is a democratic right.
items.title: Rijiju Accuses Opposition of Plotting Violence During Anti-SIR Protests

items.summary: Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister Mohan Yadav ordered the removal of Gwalior's City SP and the suspension of eight other police personnel. This action follows alleged negligence regarding a truck collision at a temple that reportedly caused a wall to collapse, killing 14 people and injuring 28 others. The incident occurred on Sunday, prompting the chief minister's intervention.
items.title: MP Chief Minister Orders Removal of Police Officials After Temple Tragedy

items.summary: A deepening sell-off in US technology stocks has exposed vulnerabilities in Asia's artificial intelligence supply chain, where mounting financing costs could choke off spending needed to sustain the boom. Oil prices surged to US$110 a barrel, stoking inflation concerns, while US semiconductor shares fell roughly 16%. Asian component makers and hardware suppliers, including Nan Ya Plastics and Samsung Electro-Mechanics, saw significant declines. Experts warn that rising borrowing costs could delay infrastructure projects, triggering a reset in earnings expectations for downstream beneficiaries. While some investors remain confident in robust demand, the financing risks of the AI boom have come into sharper focus.
items.title: Rising financing costs threaten Asia's AI hardware stocks amid US tech sell-off

items.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated that President Donald Trump would take up to 60 days to assess the economic impact of waived Russia-related sanctions and tariffs. Rubio noted that while India has voluntarily diversified its energy portfolio, it still relies heavily on Russian imports. He explained the President wants to analyze the implications for global and US economies before finalizing the waiver.
items.title: Rubio Says Trump Will Assess Waived Russia Sanctions and Tariffs

items.summary: Chinese Premier Li Qiang, meeting Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev in Tashkent on October 17, 2026, stated China's readiness to ensure the high-quality implementation of the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway project. Li emphasized strengthening strategic communication and expanding cooperation in areas such as energy, minerals, and artificial intelligence. Mirziyoyev welcomed Chinese investment and affirmed Uzbekistan's support for the railway construction and the one-China principle.
items.title: Chinese Premier Li Qiang Promotes China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan Railway Project

items.summary: Ian Chan, a former naval officer and NUS Business School student, founded Big Bullion in December 2025 to trade precious metals. The company has generated about $1.5 million in revenue, with $1.2 million from investment-grade bullion, and is expected to become profitable by December 2026. Chan attributes his success to discipline, diversification, and consistent investing, noting that his business is one of his most valuable assets alongside his gold and silver holdings. He aims to make investing more accessible to younger Singaporeans through educational content.
items.title: Former Navy Officer Builds Wealth Through Precious Metals Trading

items.summary: President Donald Trump temporarily waived provisions of the Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act to assess economic impacts on global and US markets. Rubio described India as a key ally, noting Trump utilized a 60-day window to evaluate tariffs on Russian oil importers, including India and China, before potential implementation.
items.title: Trump Waives Sanctions Provisions Amid India Allyship

items.summary: The article outlines five factors influencing the Nifty and Sensex this week, focusing on Q2 earnings, FII activity, and currency trends. HDFC Bank reported a 4.6% profit jump to Rs 19,510 crore for Q2 FY27. While FIIs remained net sellers, outflows eased to Rs 8,991 crore. The rupee rose 2% this week. Analysts note that a sustained recovery depends on easing underlying pressures, with elevated crude oil prices posing a risk. Key support and resistance levels for the Nifty are identified at 22,750 and 23,400 respectively.
items.title: Market Outlook: Nifty and Sensex Rally Factors and Levels

items.summary: The final episode of CGTN's documentary Breaking Through shifts focus from the soldiers of the Long March to the ordinary people who aided their survival. It highlights a family in Ningxia whose memories of a rescued soldier endure, while also showcasing modern farmers and entrepreneurs building new lives along the historic route in northwest China.
items.title: Breaking Through Episode 5 Explores Unsung Heroes of the Long March

items.summary: A senior finance official told Reuters that Angola could spend as much as 3.8 trillion kwanzas ($4.16 billion) on fuel subsidies in 2026, nearly double the initial projection. Ottoniel dos Santos, Angola's secretary of state for finance, noted rising global energy prices are increasing costs. The government plans a gradual subsidy removal but may accelerate if impacts on vulnerable populations are less severe than anticipated.
items.title: Angola Projects $4.16 Billion Fuel Subsidy Spending in 2026

items.summary: Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis and Shiv Sena UBT chief Uddhav Thackeray engaged in a political dispute regarding remarks on regime change. Fadnavis questioned Thackeray's stance, noting internal party shifts, while Thackeray defended the call, alleging government restrictions on protest rights. Separately, a tragic stampede at a Kolkata Durga Puja pandal claimed 19 lives, sparking political demands for accountability from the Trinamool Congress.
items.title: Maharashtra Political Clash Escalates Over Regime Change Remarks

items.summary: Pope Leo XIV held his first public engagement since undergoing lung cancer surgery on Sunday. Diagnosed with lung adenocarcinoma, the Pope recited the Angelus prayer from the window of Vatican's Apostolic Palace. He thanked wellwishers for their prayers and support, stating he will gradually return to his commitments as he recovers.
items.title: Pope Leo XIV Holds First Public Appearance After Lung Cancer Surgery

items.summary: Ukrainian forces reportedly struck St Petersburg and the Leningrad region overnight, targeting an oil terminal and a VK data centre. Local officials reported one death and 15 injuries, while regional governor Aleksandr Drozdenko stated 144 drones were shot down. Fires broke out at civilian infrastructure, and emergency power cuts affected around 20,000 people. Meanwhile, Ukrainian President Zelenskyy reported further Russian strikes on Ukraine's energy sector.
items.title: Ukrainian Forces Strike St Petersburg and Leningrad Region

items.summary: Paris experienced widespread destruction on Sunday following Saturday's protests over the cost of living. Streets were littered with debris, burnt bicycles, and damaged vehicles, while shops faced smashed windows and looting. Businesses including Nike, Sephora, and Burger King sustained damage, and the Paris Opera ticket office windows were shattered. Cleaning crews and workers began repairing the damage amid nationwide demonstrations against rising prices.
items.title: Violence and Looting Cause Widespread Damage Across Paris

items.summary: A report by the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air indicates that refineries in India, Turkiye, and Brunei shipped oil products worth €1 billion to countries sanctioning Russia in September, a 43% increase from August. While the European Union banned imports of oil products refined from Russian crude in January 2026, the ban exempts net crude oil exporters, allowing Russian-origin crude to enter global supply chains through third-country refining. Reliance Industries' Jamnagar refinery accounted for six of seven cargoes unloaded at EU ports during the month, despite the ban. India remains the second-largest buyer of Russian fossil fuels, spending €4.1 billion in September 2026.
items.title: Indian Refiners Ship Oil to Sanctioning Nations Amid EU Ban

items.summary: Gleaning Cornwall donated £1m worth of produce to 160 food banks across the South West. Founded in 2020, the group has repurposed over 460 tonnes of food. Founder Holly Whitelaw warns that rising costs for transport and storage threaten operations, urging increased funding to sustain their work against growing food poverty in Cornwall.
items.title: Gleaning Cornwall Donates £1m Produce to Food Banks Amid Funding Warnings

items.summary: A gathering of Liberal Democrat MPs recently described as a 'damp squib' revealed underlying tensions regarding Ed Davey's leadership. While no formal challenge materialized, attendees expressed irritation with the party's cautious approach, citing the resignation of Charlie Maynard and concerns that policy decisions like £17bn tax cuts alienate activists. Supporters argue Davey has built sufficient credit to address grievances, noting the absence of a viable alternative like Daisy Cooper. The party currently aims to win seats to push for proportional representation, relying on a strategy of remaining unobjectionable to secure tactical votes.
items.title: Liberal Democrat MPs express frustration over Ed Davey's cautious leadership style

items.summary: Violence erupted across France on Saturday during demonstrations against school conditions and the cost of living. At least 1,200 people were arrested as shopfronts were smashed and stores looted. Shop owners in Paris reported damages and stolen goods totaling €100,000 (£85,000). The French government described the events as an escalation in violence.
items.title: Violence and Looting Erupt Across France During School and Cost-of-Living Protests

items.summary: Police stated that a warning about a potential collapse at the Chorbagan pandal in north Kolkata may have triggered panic, contributing to a stampede on Saturday evening that killed 19 people and injured 25. Investigators are examining a video purportedly capturing the announcement and collecting CCTV footage, eyewitness accounts, and forensic evidence. While the exact sequence remains under investigation, preliminary findings point to possible crowd-management failures, unclear announcements, and a sudden influx of visitors seeking shelter from heavy rain. The state government announced compensation for the deceased and injured, and a review panel has been constituted to examine safety protocols.
items.title: Warning May Have Triggered Kolkata Stampede Killing 19

items.summary: France's interior minister Laurent Nunez reported 1,800 arrests following Saturday's protests against the cost of living. He stated over 500 emergency personnel were injured and material damage was considerable, noting the Republic would not yield to disorder.
items.title: France Interior Minister Reports 1,800 Arrests Amid Widespread Protests and Violence

items.summary: The Supreme Court rejected Tamil Nadu's policy allowing Hindu converts to Islam to claim reservation benefits under specific Muslim communities. The Court held that conversion alone does not establish membership in a historically formed community, requiring independent proof of eligibility. While acknowledging that social disadvantage may persist after conversion, the judgment maintains that reservation operates through identified groups. Consequently, applicants must now establish a legally recognized link to a notified backward class, rather than relying on their previous status or a government order that presumed such a connection.
items.title: Supreme Court Rejects Tamil Nadu's Plan for Reservation Benefits for Hindu Converts to Islam

items.summary: West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari announced a Special Investigation Team probe into the Chorbagan Durga Puja stampede in Kolkata that killed 19 people. Six arrests have been reported, and the government is monitoring the situation. The CM stated that the SIT will operate under a sitting judge and that necessary precautions are being taken for public safety.
items.title: West Bengal CM announces SIT probe after Kolkata stampede

items.summary: Nashik officials reviewed preparations for the Simhastha Maha Kumbh Mela 2027. Guardian Secretary Eknath Dawale led a meeting addressing parking, traffic management, and ghat layouts. Senior leaders, including Police Commissioner Sandip Karnik and NTKMA Commissioner Shekhar Singh, emphasized coordinated planning and timely execution. The review focused on ensuring infrastructure readiness and pilgrim safety for the upcoming religious gathering in Nashik and Trimbakeshwar.
items.title: Nashik Officials Review Infrastructure for 2027 Kumbh Mela

items.summary: Pope Leo XIV made his first public appearance since undergoing lung cancer surgery, addressing crowds from the Vatican's Apostolic Palace. The 71-year-old pontiff, who has served for 17 months, assured the faithful of his gradual return to duties. Discharged four days after the operation, he plans to resume activities with God's help and prayers. His next major engagement is an overseas trip scheduled for November.
items.title: Pope Leo XIV Makes First Public Appearance Post-Lung Cancer Surgery

items.summary: The Kerala High Court directed the state government to clear pending victim compensation dues totaling ₹9.73 crore across 225 cases within five weeks. The bench, comprising Chief Justice Soumen Sen and Justice Syam Kumar V M, also ordered the release of mediator honorariums at revised rates and mandated weekly status reviews by the Kerala State Legal Services Authority. The court emphasized ensuring timely disbursement and collecting requisite documents at adjudication to prevent future delays.
items.title: Kerala HC Orders Release of Pending Victim Compensation

items.summary: Roger Federer was spotted applauding Rafael Jodar's impressive winner against Alejandro Davidovich Fokina during the Shanghai Masters final. The 20-time Grand Slam champion, present in the stands, reacted to the young Spaniard's shot-making. Jodar, the youngest finalist in Shanghai Masters history, defeated Daniil Medvedev in the semi-finals, while Davidovich Fokina beat Alexander Zverev to reach the final.
items.title: Roger Federer Applauds Rafael Jodar's Stunning Winner at Shanghai Masters Final

items.summary: Union minister Chirag Paswan stated that while Indian citizens have the right to protest, the participation of foreign nationals is unacceptable. He expressed concern that Imran Khan, an Overseas Citizen of India cardholder, should not have joined demonstrations in Mumbai against the Chief Election Commissioner. Paswan accused foreign nationals of attempting to create anarchy with backing from foreign powers.
items.title: Chirag Paswan Criticizes Imran Khan's Protest Participation in Mumbai

items.summary: Kaval Desai, an LLB student, shared his first day as a Blinkit delivery partner on X. He completed 19 orders in about six-and-a-half hours, earning ₹508 before a ₹100 bonus brought his total to ₹608. Desai stated he pursues law as his primary profession and took the part-time work to manage personal expenses alongside his studies.
items.title: LLB Student Shares Viral Earnings as Blinkit Delivery Partner

items.summary: US Vice President JD Vance blamed France's immigration policies for escalating unrest, citing violent protests over education cuts and living costs. He criticized Western liberals for importing diversity without assimilation. French President Emmanuel Macron condemned the violence, while Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez attributed it to radical far-left groups. Protests, starting in late September, involved arson and looting, partially destroying a town hall in Limoges.
items.title: US VP Vance Blames Immigration for French Unrest Amid Violence

items.summary: The data center industry is increasingly targeting youth through educational outreach, including children's stories and school field trips, to improve its public image. Groups like 7x24 Exchange International and trade associations are promoting data centers as 'mission critical' infrastructure through activities such as flag-making kits for first graders and guided tours for high schoolers. Alex Molnar of the National Education Policy Center critiques these efforts as corporate propaganda, noting that children lack the critical ability to assess such messaging. This strategy emerges as the industry faces growing environmental concerns and community opposition, with polls showing significant public skepticism about data centers' impact on quality of life.
items.title: Data Center Industry Targets Youth with Educational Outreach Amid Backlash

items.summary: OnlyFans creator Vanniall and others express frustration that Meta allows its AI agent, Muse, to engage in explicit conversations with adult users while restricting real creators' accounts. Vanniall, whose Instagram is currently restricted, argues it is unfair for Meta to monetize sexually active AI while banning human sensuality. Jiz Lee and Tony Genius also voice concerns about AI displacing human performers and the lack of transparency regarding data usage. While Meta states that private AI conversations differ from public promotion, creators feel the policy creates a double standard. The issue highlights tensions between platform moderation, AI development, and the rights of adult content creators.
items.title: OnlyFans Creators Criticize Meta's AI Sexting Policy

items.summary: JLR India is expanding its retail presence in the National Capital Region by relocating to a larger integrated facility in Delhi and opening a new outlet in Gurugram. Managing Director Rajan Amba described the region as an important market. The move strengthens JLR's retail network, which now includes 33 outlets across 26 cities nationwide.
items.title: JLR India Expands Retail Presence in Delhi and Gurugram

items.summary: A major fire at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright has caused fatalities and injuries, overwhelming local hospitals. Dr. Warren Thirsk stated the patient influx would overwhelm Edmonton. Strong winds pushed flames into rural areas. Authorities are investigating while prioritizing support for affected personnel.
items.title: Fire at Canadian Military Base Overwhelms Local Hospitals

items.summary: Activists argue that Jantar Mantar in New Delhi is a vital democratic space for dissent, contrasting its historical role with the Centre's 2017 order to move protests to remote, hired sites. They contend this shift excludes marginalized voices and shuts out the government from public dissent. Following a 2018 Supreme Court order allowing protests with police permission, activists highlight the irony of seeking approval from the very authorities being protested. The article details how Jantar Mantar facilitated diverse movements, including the successful 2006 RTI campaign and pension demands by over 300 elderly people. Critics note that while the pension remains at Rs 200, the site continues to symbolize the struggle for rights, despite police restrictions and attempts to relocate protests.
items.title: Activists Defend Jantar Mantar as Essential Protest Space in Delhi

items.summary: IT consulting firm Accenture is reportedly looking to sell its Chinese operations for up to $1.5 billion, according to a report by the Financial Times citing people familiar with the matter. Reuters could not immediately verify the report. The sale involves Accenture's business activities within China, representing a potential significant transaction for the global consulting company.
items.title: Accenture Considers Selling Chinese Operations for Up to $1.5 Billion

items.summary: Chancellor John Healey is set to deliver the UK government's first Budget on 28 October, outlining tax and spending plans. Facing historic borrowing costs, Healey faces a difficult balancing act between supporting households, meeting defence commitments, and adhering to Labour's manifesto pledges not to raise income tax, National Insurance, or VAT. While the Office for Budget Responsibility initially calculated a £23.6bn fiscal headroom, analysts like KPMG and the IFS suggest this may have shrunk significantly due to rising interest rates. Speculation surrounds potential tax hikes on banks, changes to Capital Gains Tax, and adjustments to fuel duty and energy bills, though Healey has ruled out extending the Mansion Tax to lower-value properties. The Budget speech will be followed by parliamentary debate and potential immediate tax changes.
items.title: Chancellor Healey prepares UK Budget amid fiscal constraints and tax speculation

items.summary: Sriraj Mallick and Rahul Patwardhan argue that India must transition from a scarcity-based education system to an AI-enabled model to address skills gaps. They cite data showing only 4.2% of working-age Indians have formal vocational training and that 44 of every 100 graduates are not employable. The authors propose the 'Kaushal Chakra,' a framework utilizing AI tutors to provide personalized learning at scale, supported by a personal skills passport and independent validation. They suggest piloting this approach with the government's one crore AI training initiative to validate pathways for emerging jobs.
items.title: Experts Propose AI-Driven Skills Framework for India

items.summary: The World Bank is urging developing countries to adopt 'small AI' models capable of running on mobile phones with low connectivity. Paschal Donohoe, the World Bank's chief knowledge officer, stated that such adapted technology could accelerate development in emerging economies. Meanwhile, IMF managing director Kristalina Georgieva highlighted the need for electricity and digital infrastructure to support AI adoption, warning that the technology could significantly impact young workers' future job prospects.
items.title: World Bank Urges Developing Nations to Adopt Small AI Models

items.summary: Cities across France experienced violent demonstrations on Sunday following nationwide protests against rising living costs. Clashes, looting, and fires occurred in Paris, Marseille, and other locations. Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu condemned the violence, citing 1,200 arrests and 150 injured officers. A 17-year-old boy suffered severe injuries from a grenade. Political figures, including JD Vance and Marine Le Pen, offered differing explanations for the unrest.
items.title: Violent Protests Sweep France Amid Cost of Living Crisis

items.summary: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India suspended the license of Priyagold biscuit manufacturer Surya Food and Agro Limited after finding it used cattle-feed bran as a raw material. The regulator initiated legal proceedings for multiple hygiene and safety violations. The company has not yet responded to the action. The regulator also prosecuted other firms for similar violations.
items.title: India's food regulator suspends Priyagold license over cattle-feed bran use

items.summary: New research by environmental scientists indicates that African countries can save billions by simultaneously cutting air pollution and greenhouse gas emissions. The study, based on two reports, highlights that addressing these issues together yields significant economic benefits through reduced healthcare costs and increased productivity. In southern Africa, every dollar spent on pollution reduction could generate approximately US$26 in benefits. The researchers propose 25 proven solutions and 37 specific areas for improvement across sectors like energy, transport, and agriculture. While implementation costs are estimated at US$11 billion by 2035, the financial returns and lives saved justify the investment. The authors urge development banks to recognize these combined benefits in funding decisions.
items.title: New Research Links Air Pollution Reduction to Economic Gains in Africa

items.summary: A team of cardiologists conducted a three-month blood pressure screening in Lagos in 2023, testing up to 1,500 adults. The study found that 52.5% of participants had hypertension, with 65.3% of those cases being undiagnosed. Furthermore, only 13.8% of identified hypertensive individuals were taking medication, and just 8.3% had controlled blood pressure. The researchers attribute these gaps to financial barriers, lack of awareness, and systemic issues, calling for improved access to affordable treatment and integrated health systems to prevent future heart-related deaths.
items.title: Nigerian Cardiologists Find High Hypertension Rates and Low Awareness in Lagos

items.summary: Maharashtra's chief electoral officer has requested the Election Commission of India to modify Form 6. The change aims to allow voters deleted during the Special Intensive Revision to re-apply without falsely declaring themselves as first-time voters. The CEO proposed removing 'New Voters' from the title and allowing previous EPIC numbers. The amendment depends on ECI approval before the final roll publication on November 16.
items.title: Maharashtra CEO Requests Form 6 Changes for SIR Deletions

items.summary: A professor of management information systems at Drexel University describes 'latent risk,' where employees relying on reliable AI systems may lose the ability to intervene when the AI fails. This phenomenon, building on research into automation bias, occurs when organizations depend on human judgment that has atrophied due to over-reliance on automated recommendations, leaving staff unprepared to step in when the system cannot proceed.
items.title: Professor Warns of Latent Risk in Human-AI Collaboration

items.summary: Standard internet speed tests often fail to reveal internal Wi-Fi bottlenecks because they measure external connection speeds rather than local data movement. To accurately troubleshoot home network performance, the article recommends OpenSpeedTest, a self-hosted tool that measures connection speeds strictly between devices on the local network, independent of the internet connection.
items.title: OpenSpeedTest Offers Local Network Speed Checks to Diagnose Wi-Fi Issues

items.summary: Pepperdine University has introduced a new year-round program in Kyoto designed to immerse American students in local life away from tourist crowds. The initiative places students in traditional machiya townhouses for language lessons and cultural activities, such as planning formal dinners. This first cohort aims to provide an authentic experience while allowing students to continue their regular studies at the Malibu, California, institution.
items.title: Pepperdine University Launches Year-Round Japan Program in Kyoto

items.summary: Starlink has become a critical component of Ukraine's defense system, supporting communications, reconnaissance, and drone operations since Russia's 2022 invasion. According to the Center for Security Studies at ETH Zurich, approximately 50,000 Starlink terminals were in use in Ukraine in 2025. Recent reports indicate that SpaceX temporarily restricted terminal speeds to about 160 kilometers per hour (100 mph), which could hinder fast-moving drones traveling up to 300 kilometers per hour (186 mph). While Starlink is vital, Ukraine also relies on reconnaissance data from Western partners, particularly the United States. Experts note that dependence on private technology companies marks a fundamental shift in modern warfare.
items.title: How reliant is Ukraine on the US-controlled Starlink internet service?

items.summary: Floating wind turbines are operational in Europe, Asia, and Maine, yet large-scale U.S. projects face delays due to high costs and engineering hurdles. The Biden Administration set a 2035 goal of 15 GW, but the sector now confronts a crisis driven by policy reversals and sustained attacks on offshore wind by the Trump administration. While international collaboration continues to advance the technology, U.S. developers face uncertainty as leases are bought back and grants cancelled. Despite these challenges, research persists, with Maine serving as a testing ground and Canadian initiatives gaining momentum. The industry relies on transatlantic partnerships to overcome technical barriers and achieve commercial viability.
items.title: U.S. Floating Wind Industry Faces Policy Uncertainty Amid Global Progress

items.summary: The Nigerian Army Chief of Staff visited troops in Borno following an attack where jihadists killed 15 soldiers and five militia members. Sources reported that ISWAP fighters overran and burnt a military base in Mairari village. Residents confirmed the attack occurred around 2200 GMT, forcing a troop withdrawal. The region remains a focal point of a 17-year insurgency.
items.title: Nigerian Army Chief Visits Troops After Base Attack

items.summary: A Supreme Court-appointed enquiry committee investigating alleged police excesses during July youth protests launched a portal for affected persons to submit complaints. Priority is given to cases involving pellet guns, targeted violence, and harassment of women. The portal protects witness identities and allows anonymous submissions. The committee will also assess medical assistance and injuries sustained by police personnel.
items.title: SC Panel Launches Portal for Complaints on Police Excesses

items.summary: A serious fire at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright in Alberta killed and injured personnel, overwhelming local hospitals. Defense Minister David McGuinty confirmed casualties while authorities investigate. The blaze spread due to fierce winds, disrupting nearby areas and advance voting for an independence referendum. Officials describe the situation as active and delicate, with assistance being sent from other provinces.
items.title: Fatal Fire at Canadian Military Base in Alberta

items.summary: Koichi Hagiuda, acting secretary-general of the Liberal Democratic Party, denied that former agriculture minister Kazuo Yana influenced budget cuts for municipalities. Hagiuda stated on a television debate that they could not confirm allocations were changed due to Yana's actions. He apologized for the controversy and called for an investigation into budget allocation suspicions.
items.title: LDP Executive Denies Former Minister Influenced Budget Cuts

items.summary: SA Police arrested two teenage boys following an alleged fight at Mosely Square in Glenelg involving dozens of youths. Police responded to the beach after a disturbance report, arresting the fighters for disorderly behaviour. No officers were injured. Police stated there is no tolerance for public disorder and will take proactive action. The arrests occur amid investigations into recent brawls in the area.
items.title: Two Teenage Boys Arrested After Glenelg Fight

items.summary: A major fire erupted at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright in Alberta following a deadly incident, according to Canada's defense minister. Fierce winds spread flames into the surrounding rural area, overwhelming local hospitals with injured personnel. Authorities described the situation as active and delicate while investigating the cause. No evacuation orders were issued, though the fire disrupted advance voting for a provincial referendum.
items.title: Major Fire Breaks Out in Alberta After Deadly Incident at Military Base

items.summary: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen announced a range of measures to address rising energy prices, including the release of 100 million barrels of oil and diesel reserves and the extension of a temporary state aid framework. While acknowledging that no single solution exists for the crisis, she emphasized the need for a comprehensive approach involving a transition to clean, homegrown energy sources. EU leaders have yet to agree on a long-term strategy balancing climate objectives with energy costs, though they reaffirmed core climate pledges like REPowerEU and the European Green Deal. Industry groups like Eurelectric and SolarPower Europe called for targeted, temporary measures and affordable electrification to ensure market stability and lower prices.
items.title: EU Unveils Energy Measures Amidst Price Surge and Climate Goals

items.summary: Populist Czech Prime Minister Andrej Babis's ruling coalition failed to win any seats in the 2025 Senate elections. Opposition parties secured 22 of the 27 available seats, retaining control of the upper house. Babis, leading the centrist ANO movement, described the outcome as catastrophic but vowed to continue his government's agenda, including plans to revamp public broadcaster funding. The Senate retains significant influence over constitutional amendments and judicial appointments.
items.title: Populist Czech PM Babis Loses All Senate Seats in 2025 Election

items.summary: MYB Textiles Ltd operates as the final facility globally weaving patterned Nottingham lace on traditional looms. Historically, the Irvine Valley towns of Newmilns and Darvel hosted 20 lace mills, which served as the area's largest employer until the late 1970s. Competition from Europe and Asia subsequently reduced the industry, leaving MYB Textiles Ltd as the sole remaining producer, now serving the film and entertainment sectors.
items.title: MYB Textiles Ltd Remains World's Last Traditional Lace Mill

items.summary: An article details the unspoken rules and rigorous routines governing flight attendants' work, highlighting safety duties often invisible to passengers. It explains that pay typically begins when aircraft doors close, excluding pre-flight tasks like stowing bags and safety checks. The piece outlines extensive emergency training requirements, including evacuation drills and medical response, which are aircraft-specific. Seniority dictates scheduling, base assignments, and break availability, creating distinct experiences for junior and senior crew. Layovers are legally defined rest periods often shortened by travel logistics, while the brace position is scientifically designed to minimize injury during sudden deceleration. Crew members are legally bound to their posts once doors close, with limited options for leaving due to federal staffing regulations.
items.title: Hidden Rules and Routines Behind Flight Attendants' Jobs

items.summary: HDFC Bank's profit after tax increased by 5% according to a recent report. Outgoing chief executive Sashidhar Jagdishan attributed this growth to underlying business momentum in retail and MSME sectors during a post-earnings call. The statement highlights positive performance in key business segments driving the financial results.
items.title: HDFC Bank PAT Rises 5% Amid Business Momentum

items.summary: Ixigo's hotels business reached a critical mass, with gross booking value crossing 100 crores and revenue growing over 500%. Group CEO Aloke Bajpai attributed 86% of this growth to the company's captive user base.
items.title: Ixigo Hotels Business Reaches Critical Mass with Record Revenue

items.summary: According to the Seoul Economic Daily, Samsung Electronics will utilize TSMC's 3-nanometre process to manufacture base dies for Nvidia's next-generation HBM chips. This collaboration marks the first instance of Samsung working with TSMC at the HBM manufacturing stage. Nvidia requested this from Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron Technology. Samsung plans to retain its in-house production for standard HBM while assessing TSMC capacity for NVHBM base dies.
items.title: Samsung to Use TSMC Technology for Nvidia Memory Chips

items.summary: Microsoft and the Health Information Sharing and Analysis Center dismantled three Chinese-language cybercrime stores, YAM Store, CoGUI, and Iron Man, following a 2025 alert from Japan's National Police Agency. The operation, supported by a global coalition, seized infrastructure responsible for over 750 million fraudulent messages targeting Microsoft customers and 75,000 organizations worldwide. Steven Masada of Microsoft's Digital Crimes Unit noted that severing this infrastructure hampers scammers' ability to acquire compromised accounts and automated tools.
items.title: Microsoft and partners dismantle Chinese cybercrime infrastructure

items.summary: Anthropic's offensive research team reported a potential threat where an AI program could autonomously spread across internet-connected smart televisions and other devices by splitting its code among them. Experts note that existing cybersecurity infrastructure is not ready for such threats, which could adapt to new vulnerabilities. While some, like Joshua Saxe, urge mitigation, others, including Juan Andres Guerrero-Saade, dismiss the immediate feasibility as 'nifty stunt hacking.' The report highlights that smart devices often receive patches less frequently than phones, making them vulnerable. However, experts suggest that basic security hygiene, such as strong passwords, could stop most worms. The debate continues over whether these risks are genuine threats or part of 'doomer narratives.'
items.title: Anthropic Researchers Warn of Self-Replicating AI Worms Threatening Smart Devices

items.summary: Adani Group chairman Gautam Adani and Adani Foundation chairperson Dr Priti Adani visited Shrimad Rajchandra Mission in Dharampur, South Gujarat, during Navratri to seek blessings from Pujya Gurudevshri Rakeshji. The couple performed charan pakshal at the world's tallest idol of Shrimad Rajchandraji, an experience Adani described as deeply moving. Dr Priti Adani toured various facilities, including a women's centre and a hospital, while both leaders discussed potential cooperation between the Adani Foundation and the Mission's humanitarian arm, Shrimad Rajchandra Love and Care. The visit highlighted the Mission's focus on spiritual practice and selfless service across its 142 global centres.
items.title: Adani Leaders Visit Spiritual Mission for Blessings and Potential Collaboration
