items.summary: Microsoft has withdrawn from a planned AI datacentre project in Loughton, Essex, citing power supply concerns. The development, led by Nscale and supported by the UK government, was intended to be the country's largest sovereign AI datacentre. Microsoft, expected to be the anchor tenant, informed Nscale it was ending the agreement. This move leaves Nscale without its only publicly announced customer for the site, potentially undermining its plans to float on Wall Street with a valuation of $35bn (£26bn). Nscale remains committed to the project and is exploring alternative power sources.
items.title: Microsoft Exits Essex AI Datacentre Project Over Power Supply Worries

items.summary: Violent protests in France escalated into widespread looting and vandalism on October 17, targeting stores belonging to Apple, Louis Vuitton, and Hermès. Demonstrations occurred in cities including Paris, Marseille, Bordeaux, and Lille, marked by arson and clashes with police. The French Interior Ministry reported 272 arrests by 3 pm. President Emmanuel Macron condemned the violence, warning of legal consequences, while trade unions and the government disputed protest turnout figures.
items.title: Violent Protests in France Target Luxury Stores Amid Cost of Living Crisis

items.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang expressed optimism regarding the AI market, stating that technology benefits will soon outweigh investor concerns. Speaking to Bloomberg's Emily Chang in Berlin, Huang noted that the current market rout is temporary and that AI will positively impact every industry and country. He emphasized that while news may be choppy, it does not alter the fundamental long-term value of the technology.
items.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Optimistic on AI Market Despite Recent Turmoil

items.summary: A heavy truck ploughed into devotees at the Sheetla Mata Temple fair in Gwalior around 1.30 am on Sunday, killing at least 16 people and injuring 26 others. Questions arose regarding how the trucks reached the shrine on a route closed to all vehicles. While accounts vary on whether brakes failed or trucks broke through barricades, officials stated drivers relying on GPS were directed to the restricted road. Chief Minister Dr Mohan Yadav removed the city superintendent of police and suspended eight others pending a detailed inquiry. The Prime Minister expressed condolences and announced financial aid for the victims.
items.title: Truck Accident at Gwalior Temple Fair Kills Dozens

items.summary: Apple stated that demand for the new iPhone Duo is extraordinary following delivery delays extending into January. The company continues accepting orders while preparing for in-store experiences. Analysts suggest sales could exceed 14 million units, potentially boosting Apple's fiscal 2027 revenue to $28 billion. Apple shares rose 0.43% to $343.46 on Friday.
items.title: Apple Reports Extraordinary Demand for New Foldable iPhone Amid Shipping Delays

items.summary: China showcased its first homegrown 100,000-card AI supercluster, named Dawning 8000, at the WAIC 2026 and CCF National Annual Conference in July 2026. The system integrates supercomputing and AI computing to handle scientific simulations and model training. Officials demonstrated its potential to simulate a universe spanning tens of billions of light-years and create a digital twin of the human brain.
items.title: China Unveils 100,000-Card AI Supercluster at 2026 Conferences

items.summary: Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav accused the BJP of conspiring to manipulate electoral rolls by adding fake votes and deleting genuine ones ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. Speaking at the SP headquarters in Lucknow, Yadav urged party workers to remain vigilant at polling booths. He questioned the need for the Election Commission's Special Summary Revision (SSR) following the recent Special Intensive Revision (SIR), alleging the process benefits the BJP. Yadav also criticized the BJP government's record on governance, citing inflation, unemployment, and alleged corruption, while claiming the party protects land grabbers and targets the PDA community. He further alleged that the BJP could consolidate power through its 'One Nation, One Election' proposal.
items.title: Akhilesh Yadav Accuses BJP of Electoral Manipulation Ahead of 2027 UP Elections

items.summary: CGTN reporter Liu Jiaxin rode the 58-seat electric sightseeing boat Star of East Lake in Ningde to examine the growth of electric propulsion. The vessel travels 33 km on a single charge and reduces annual CO₂ emissions by roughly 100 tonnes compared to diesel equivalents. The report suggests these technologies are paving the way for zero-carbon harbors and future electric ocean-going vessels.
items.title: Liu Jiaxin explores electric boat expansion in Ningde

items.summary: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Home Minister Amit Shah, and Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar of orchestrating vote theft and corruption. Speaking in Goa, he claimed their 'expiry date' is near and urged voters to support Congress in the 2027 elections. Gandhi noted facing over 45 defamation cases from these leaders but stated no case exists against him for his allegations. He also highlighted student protests in Delhi linked to concerns over vote theft and rising education costs.
items.title: Rahul Gandhi Accuses BJP Leaders of Vote Theft and Corruption

items.summary: CleanTechnica author Zach compares Tesla CEO Elon Musk's Roadster reveal to the Florida Department of Transportation's plans for an aerial highway network. While the state has allocated $197 million in federal grant money for electric vehicle chargers, Musk demonstrated a flying prototype, which Steve Hanley called the stupidest display he has witnessed. The article suggests Musk's actions are a PR stunt to boost wavering stock prices rather than expanding the Supercharger network. Meanwhile, businesses like Buc-ees and Wawa received funding to cover about 80% of charger costs, with the remaining 20% required from them. The author criticizes both Musk and Florida for prioritizing imagination over practical infrastructure.
items.title: Tesla Roadster Stunt and Florida Flying Car Plans Draw Criticism

items.summary: ICICI Bank reported a 20% surge in profit attributed to Net Interest Income (NII), while core profitability declined slightly due to FCNR(B) impacts. Outgoing CEO Sashidhar Jagdishan highlighted underlying business momentum in retail and MSME sectors during a post-earnings call, noting these metrics as key drivers of the financial performance.
items.title: ICICI Bank Profit Rises 20% Driven by NII Growth

items.summary: Croatian Prime Minister Andrej Plenkovic met with Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi in Zagreb on October 17, 2026. Plenkovic expressed Croatia's willingness to deepen cooperation within the China-CEEC framework. Wang emphasized China's commitment to strengthening ties and noted the upcoming 15th anniversary of the mechanism as a chance to revitalize mutually beneficial cooperation. Both leaders discussed trade relations and regional stability in the Western Balkans.
items.title: Croatian PM and Chinese FM Call for Deeper Bilateral Cooperation

items.summary: China strongly condemned Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and other lawmakers for sending ritual offerings to the Yasukuni Shrine. A spokesperson for the Chinese Embassy stated the shrine enshrines 14 Class-A war criminals and symbolizes militarism. China urged Japan to reflect on its history, face wartime responsibilities, and break with militarism to earn regional trust.
items.title: China Condemns Japanese Politicians Over Yasukuni Shrine Offerings

items.summary: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) directed food companies to maintain appropriate temperature conditions during the storage and transport of perishable items like meat and paneer to safeguard public health. The regulator cited risks of microbial growth and spoilage, emphasizing compliance with existing regulations. It also instructed state FDAs to enforce strict vigilance against violations and ensure hygienic vehicles are used throughout the supply chain.
items.title: FSSAI Orders Temperature Control for Perishable Food Transport and Storage

items.summary: Clashes erupted in Milan, Turin, and Bologna during protests against rising living costs in Italy. In Milan, 50 people were detained following violent confrontations with police, while 25 others were injured, including ten officers. Turin saw 12 detentions and 10 injuries, and Bologna reported seven arrests. Demonstrators threw objects and set fires, prompting police to use tear gas and water cannons. Political figures, including Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni and Mayor Giuseppe Sala, condemned the violence while acknowledging the underlying economic grievances. Meloni urged the opposition not to exploit the unrest, while Sala emphasized the need for wisdom in addressing the crisis.
items.title: Italian Cities See Cost-of-Living Protests Turn Violent

items.summary: The Delhi High Court quashed lookout circulars against two Authum officials, Amit Dangi and Sanjay Dangi, in a money laundering investigation involving Reliance Commercial Finance and Reliance Home Finance. Justice Madhu Jain ruled that continued restrictions on their travel were unwarranted, directing them to cooperate with investigators and inform authorities before foreign travel. The Enforcement Directorate must update records accordingly.
items.title: Delhi High Court Quashes Lookout Circulars Against Authum Officials

items.summary: The Ayodhya Trust announced an increase in daily online passes from 975 to 2,000 and a seven-stage release schedule up to 90 days in advance. Approved by General Secretary Swami Govinddev Giri Ji Maharaj, the measures aim to reduce intermediary dependence. A verification system will confirm bookings within 24 to 48 hours, while same-day Tatkal passes remain instant. Passes remain free, and the Trust advises booking only through authorized channels.
items.title: Ayodhya Trust Expands Online Darshan Pass Availability and Security

items.summary: Speaking at a rally in Goa, Rahul Gandhi asserted that the government of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah faces an imminent end. He alleged that the country's soul has understood the truth behind their leadership and that electoral manipulation, including vote theft, has occurred in states such as MP, Haryana, Karnataka, Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra, Bengal, and Assam. Gandhi noted that while there are more than 45 defamation cases against him, none have been filed for calling Modi a vote thief, suggesting this silence proves the allegations. He stated that the youth are up in arms and that the government's rule will end once the people reclaim the republic. The Congress leader is currently participating in the Goy Rakhonn Yatra to highlight issues like land grabbing and corruption ahead of Goa's expected polls in 2027.
items.title: Rahul Gandhi Claims Government's Expiry Date Is Near Amid Vote Theft Allegations

items.summary: The Election Commission faces intense scrutiny following recent reversals regarding the Special Intensive Revision and its ECI net platform. These actions have raised questions about their legality and transparency amid nationwide protests over voter deletions. The Federal interviewed Anjali Bharadwaj, Javed Ansari, and Nikhil Jain to explore whether these measures can restore public trust in the electoral process or if the panel must be held accountable.
items.title: Election Commission faces scrutiny over voter deletion reversals and public trust

items.summary: Chinese brand LEAPTING unveiled the Auto-Navigation Forklift Robot (AFR) at a Dubai conference. The battery-powered robot uses GPS, LiDAR, and computer vision to handle solar modules without human operators. It claims to mount modules every 40 seconds with high accuracy, suitable for various terrains.
items.title: LEAPTING Unveils Autonomous Solar Forklift Robot

items.summary: A disagreement has emerged between Shiv Sena (Uddhav Balasaheb Thackeray) and the Congress regarding the allocation of nominated corporator posts in the Nashik Municipal Corporation. While Shiv Sena proposed a two-year Standing Committee membership, Congress insisted on a nominated seat. Despite previous agreements and MP Sanjay Raut's advice for internal discussion, the parties remain at an impasse as political circles watch the dispute closely.
items.title: Shiv Sena and Congress Clash Over Nashik Corporator Seat

items.summary: Shiv Sena Rajya Sabha MP Milind Deora attributed recent unrest in France to years of failed migration policies and a lack of accountability. He urged European nations to tighten immigration rules and deport migrants who refuse to integrate. Reuters reported that demonstrations against rising living costs and declining public services spiralled into severe violence, marking some of the worst incidents France has seen in decades.
items.title: Milind Deora Blames Failed Migration Policies for France Unrest

items.summary: Raphael Glucksmann secured the Socialist Party's presidential nomination for the 2027 election with 66% of the vote in the first round, defeating expectations of a two-round contest. However, his candidacy faces significant challenges, including a flour bomb attack and skepticism from young voters who currently favor Jean-Luc Melenchon. Polls suggest Glucksmann may struggle to gain traction, projecting only 10–11% support compared to Melenchon's 18%. Glucksmann has called for a clear break from the far left, a stance that contrasts with the party's need to win over Melenchon's supporters to overcome the Socialists' poor performance in 2022.
items.title: Raphael Glucksmann Wins Socialist Primary Amidst Youth Skepticism and Far-Left Tensions

items.summary: Heavy rainfall exceeding 20 cm in 24 hours battered Chennai during the northeast monsoon, with Parrys recording the highest amount at 36.3 cm. The Tamil Nadu government has directed relief efforts, engaging nearly 15,000 staff and deploying pumps to manage inundated areas. The Meteorological Department attributes the rain to an upper air cyclonic circulation, while forecasts indicate continued heavy rainfall and thunderstorms across several districts.
items.title: Heavy Rainfall Hits Chennai During Northeast Monsoon

items.summary: At the World Bank and IMF Annual Meetings in Bangkok, delegates discussed the economic challenges facing developing nations. Wayne Henry of the Planning Institute of Jamaica highlighted geopolitical and climate vulnerabilities affecting the Caribbean region. Leaders argued that a strategy combining fiscal consolidation with aggressive investment in digital connectivity is essential for developing economies to join the technology recovery and safeguard vulnerable citizens amidst rising energy costs and climate disasters.
items.title: IMF Meeting Calls for Digital Investment to Aid Developing Nations

items.summary: Official data from the Office for National Statistics indicates that opposite-sex couples in England and Wales are increasingly divorcing after 20 years or more. Recent figures show over a quarter of such divorces occurred after this duration, surpassing the traditional five-to-nine-year peak. Experts attribute this trend to couples staying together for children's sake, though rising living costs also discourage splitting up.
items.title: Marriages in England and Wales More Likely to End After Two Decades

items.summary: Gross redemptions from equity mutual fund schemes rose 19% to ₹1.25 lakh crore in the September quarter, driven by early investors withdrawing funds due to global uncertainty. Small-cap and mid-cap redemptions also increased, while hybrid funds saw a 12% rise. Market indices like the Nifty 50 and Sensex declined significantly during the period, with foreign outflows and rising oil prices cited as contributing factors.
items.title: Equity Mutual Fund Redemptions Rise Amid Global Uncertainty

items.summary: An unnamed speaker alleged that Gyanesh Kumar, Amit Shah, and Narendra Modi orchestrate vote theft, noting they face over 45 defamation cases without complaint. Separately, police in Karnal detained two individuals after a bus attack linked to a parking dispute, ruling out a hate crime. The incident gained attention via viral video, prompting Omar Abdullah's response. Other news covered a pandal stampede and political exchanges between Himanta Biswa Sarma and Akhilesh Yadav.
items.title: Speaker Allegates Vote Theft Amidst Kashmir Bus Attack Report

items.summary: Activist Ratna Singh alleges that the bail hearing of CJP leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka was delayed because the Special Executive Magistrate failed to arrive. Singh stated that four sureties were rejected on vague grounds. The leaders, currently in judicial custody, claim they unfurled the national flag and warned of legal action if not released by Sunday.
items.title: CJP Leaders Bail Hearing Delayed as Magistrate Fails to Arrive

items.summary: California has enacted the Home Energy Choice Act, requiring utilities to offer households facing service line replacements a choice between installing new gas lines or receiving financial incentives to switch to all-electric equipment. This legislation, championed by Merrian Borgeson of the Natural Resources Defense Council, aims to prevent unnecessary gas infrastructure investment and reduce costs for all ratepayers. While the law mandates this option, it includes limitations such as a cap on eligible customers and an expiration date in 2035. Utilities must develop detailed frameworks for these programs by January 2028, with larger incentives planned for disadvantaged communities. Opponents argue the policy shifts costs unfairly to remaining gas users, but proponents view it as a significant step toward a carbon-neutral economy.
items.title: California Law Gives Households Choice Between Gas Line Replacement or Electrification Incentives

items.summary: Pope Leo XIV announced he will gradually resume duties following cancer surgery that removed a malignant tumor from his lung. He expressed gratitude for prayers and support during his hospitalization at Gemelli hospital. His surgeon stated there are no clinical reasons preventing his upcoming trip to South America, though histological testing is ongoing to determine if additional treatment is needed.
items.title: Pope Leo XIV Resumes Duties After Lung Cancer Surgery

items.summary: Greens senator Jordan Steele-John denied allegations of inappropriate conduct towards women, attributing the public fallout to party factionalism. He stated he is not on leave and that the matter is under internal investigation. Steele-John claimed false allegations included sexual assault, noting police found no charges. He criticized the handling of the situation by party leadership.
items.title: Greens Senator Jordan Steele-John Denies Inappropriate Conduct Allegations

items.summary: Cameroon's main opposition party MRC elected Tiriane Balbine Noah as its first female president on Saturday. She replaces Maurice Kamto, who led the party for 14 years. Noah secured over 96 per cent of the vote at a congress held in Yaoundé despite government pressure to ban the meeting. The party now aims for the 2027 local elections.
items.title: Cameroon Opposition MRC Elects First Female President Tiriane Noah

items.summary: Uttar Pradesh has initiated land acquisition for the New Noida project, targeting 37 priority villages in its first phase. Advisor Awanish Kumar Awasthi confirmed the move on Sunday. The proposed industrial city spans 209 sq km and covers 84 villages across Gautam Buddha Nagar and Bulandshahr districts, aiming to become a major manufacturing and logistics hub in the NCR.
items.title: Uttar Pradesh Begins Land Acquisition for New Noida Manufacturing Hub

items.summary: Delhi's chief electoral officer stated that approximately 26 lakh cases, representing 78.5% of 33.1 lakh flagged discrepancies, have been resolved. Verification concludes by October 29, with final rolls due November 4. The Supreme Court previously noted concerns over mechanical notice issuance. Meanwhile, protests continue against the revision process, and some states are using the Special Intensive Revision to deny ration cards and passports.
items.title: Delhi resolves most voter roll discrepancy cases amid ongoing revision concerns

items.summary: Australia defeated New Zealand by two wickets in the first women's T20 final at North Sydney Oval. The hosts survived a dramatic late collapse, securing victory with seven balls remaining. The match concluded with Australia scoring 210 while New Zealand reached 64 and 95. The series is scheduled to continue at the same venue on Tuesday.
items.title: Australia beats New Zealand in first women's T20 final

items.summary: NTPC plans to initiate feasibility studies for nuclear projects in Indian states like Madhya Pradesh, Bihar, and Odisha. Aiming for 30 GW capacity by 2047 to support a 100 GW national target, the company will assess sites based on water availability, land suitability, seismic safety, and environmental impact. Average projects will feature 1,400 MW capacity.
items.title: NTPC Plans 30 GW Nuclear Capacity by 2047

items.summary: Following cost-of-living protests that escalated into violence, businesses across France, including major supermarket chains, are recovering from widespread looting. Authorities report attacks in cities like Paris and Lyon. Carrefour CEO Alexandre Bompard stated 50 shops were targeted, predicting considerable economic consequences. Meanwhile, a journalist was assaulted while filming, and over 600 emergency responders were injured.
items.title: Businesses Recover After France Looting Spirals From Cost-of-Living Protests

items.summary: The Assam government demolished homes of over 600 Muslim families in the Lutumari Longjap Reserve Forest, claiming encroachment. Residents, including Abdul Noor, stated they were settled by the government in 1974 and challenged the evictions in court. Officials noted 547 families were evicted across three districts. Data indicates about 19,000 families were evicted under BJP rule in the last decade.
items.title: Assam Government Demolishes Homes of Muslim Families in Forest Reserve

items.summary: A delegation of European diplomats from Belgium, France, Poland, and the Catholic Church was attacked by masked Israeli settlers in the village of Taybeh near Ramallah. The assault occurred while the envoys assessed the situation regarding ongoing settler violence against Palestinians during the olive harvest. Belgian and French officials condemned the incident as appalling and called for justice. The Israeli Defense Forces also condemned the violence but noted that no soldiers were present. Conversely, the office of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu cast doubt on the reports, suggesting a coordinated smear campaign against Israel. Investigations are ongoing to establish the facts and identify those responsible.
items.title: European Diplomats Attacked by Masked Israeli Settlers in West Bank

items.summary: Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov and Saudi counterpart Prince Faisal bin Farhan voiced concern over tensions in the southern Arabian Peninsula and the Bab el-Mandeb Strait during talks in Bahrain on October 18, 2026. Speaking on the sidelines of the Russia-GCC Strategic Dialogue, the ministers emphasized the importance of maritime safety and unimpeded vessel passage. They called for rapid de-escalation and stressed that political and diplomatic means are the only way to resolve differences while respecting regional interests.
items.title: Russian and Saudi Foreign Ministers Express Concern Over Regional Tensions

items.summary: Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov stated that Moscow supports Gulf Cooperation Council efforts to prevent a return to full-scale war in the Middle East. Speaking in Bahrain, Lavrov proposed an updated collective security concept and highlighted a 45% increase in trade turnover between Russia and GCC states last year. He emphasized that regional stability is essential for economic cooperation.
items.title: Russia Backs GCC Security Efforts Amid Middle East Tensions

items.summary: France experienced widespread damage on Sunday following days of protests that escalated into riots and looting in cities including Paris, Marseille, and Lille. Demonstrators clashed with police, resulting in approximately 1,800 arrests and injuries to over 500 officers and firefighters. While initial protests were largely peaceful and focused on rising fuel prices and public services, the unrest devolved into violence where shops were ransacked and buildings set ablaze. Authorities attributed the destruction to several thousand far-left individuals and delinquents rather than the original demonstrators. Local officials described the damage to historic buildings and tourist offices as tragedies, while residents expressed fear over the impunity shown by the looters.
items.title: Riots and Looting Erupt Across French Cities Amid Protests

items.summary: A large-scale Ukrainian drone attack on Saint Petersburg killed at least one person and hospitalized five others, while sparking fires at an oil refinery and depot. Authorities reported damage to 12 housing blocks and restricted flights at Pulkovo airport. The strike occurred as Kyiv accused Russia of violating a US-announced 'energy ceasefire,' which Kyiv claims Russia has broken dozens of times. While Moscow stated air defenses shot down 144 drones, residents described the chaos and fear. The incident highlights ongoing tensions between Kyiv and Washington regarding sanctions and fuel prices.
items.title: Ukrainian Drone Attack Kills One in Saint Petersburg Amid Energy Ceasefire Dispute

items.summary: Abhijeet Dipke, founder of the Cockroach Janata Party, vowed to continue protests against the Election Commission's electoral roll verification after securing conditional bail in Delhi. He stated that his party and associates would regroup once detained leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka are released. Dipke, who was detained ahead of a rally, described the arrests as an intimidation attempt and affirmed his party's preparedness for a long battle. Legal counsel Ratna Singh challenged the arrest's legality, alleging unlawful preventive detention.
items.title: CJP Founder Vows Protest Continues After Bail

items.summary: Alejandro Davidovich Fokina defeated Rafael Jodar to win the Shanghai Masters, ending Jodar's run and securing his biggest title. The 25th-seeded Spaniard climbed to a career-high world number 13. Jodar, the youngest finalist in history, had made a blistering start but lost the decider after Fokina recovered from a break down in the second set.
items.title: Davidovich Fokina Claims Shanghai Masters Title

items.summary: Kyodo News Agency reported that Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's administration approval rating fell below 50% to 49.1%, the lowest since October. A poll conducted Oct. 17 and 18 found 57.7% of respondents felt her decision to replace farm minister Kazuo Yana came too late, while 81.5% agreed his resignation was natural.
items.title: Takaichi's Approval Rating Drops to Lowest Since Taking Office

items.summary: Chennai experienced its heaviest rainfall since Cyclone Michaung in 2023, with some areas receiving over 30 cm in a short period. The weather department warned of more showers and reviewed cloudburst possibilities. Officials urged calm while working to ensure public safety as waterlogged roads disrupted connectivity across the city.
items.title: Chennai Faces Heavy Rainfall and Cloudburst Concerns

items.summary: Residents in the Preserve at Medina subdivision in San Antonio face ongoing risks from the Thompson Callaway Spears #1 well, a plugged oil well that has leaked gas multiple times since 2006. Despite five plugging attempts by the Railroad Commission, hydrogen sulfide and methane continue to leak, causing odors, health issues like headaches, and safety concerns. The well is located near homes built in the early 2020s, with no prior disclosure to buyers. Texas lacks statewide laws requiring disclosure of legacy wells, leaving homeowners unaware of potential dangers. Regulators are conducting monitoring and reviewing a new plugging strategy, but residents remain concerned about long-term safety and liability.
items.title: Residents in San Antonio Subdivision Face Risks from Leaking Plugged Oil Well

items.summary: This article outlines a ten-step process for travelers to recover lost checked bags and secure compensation. It distinguishes between delayed and lost luggage, noting that airlines typically declare bags lost after a waiting period ranging from five to 21 days. The text advises filing a Property Irregularity Report at the airport immediately and retaining baggage claim tags. It explains that international flights under the Montreal Convention have a liability cap of 1,288 Special Drawing Rights, while U.S. domestic flights fall under Department of Transportation rules. The guide also covers reimbursement for essentials, the role of travel insurance and credit card benefits, and the option to file complaints with regulators like the DOT if claims are denied.
items.title: Guide to recovering lost luggage and filing claims

items.summary: Engineer David Mummery developed the Swimmer Turbine, a compact tidal generator designed for local coastal communities to build and install themselves. Unlike large utility-scale projects, this device can power about 30 homes and consists of roughly 20 components. Mummery founded Flex Marine Power to focus on this accessible technology after observing that existing large-scale equipment excluded local fishermen. The company secured £968,000 in funding to develop a commercial model that launches from shore and remains hidden underwater, aiming to empower coastal residents with tidal energy.
items.title: Engineer David Mummery Develops Locally Built Tidal Turbine

items.summary: Zoey Darnbrough, a 26-year-old from Dumfries and Galloway, has risen from tour guide to coordinator at Annandale Distillery. She joined the site three-and-a-half years ago after initially being unaware of the local industry. Darnbrough aims to change perceptions of the region's heritage and tourism, noting its quiet strength and vast attractions. She remains committed to the area despite challenges, hoping to inspire others to stay.
items.title: Zoey Darnbrough Rises in Scottish Whisky Industry

items.summary: Richard Socher, CEO of Recursive and You.com, argues that AI's most meaningful application is automating scientific discovery. He suggests a 'Eureka machine' that combines human knowledge to solve major problems. Socher notes that while chatbots dominate headlines, AI's historical significance lies in science, citing recent Nobel Prizes won by AI pioneers in chemistry and physics. He believes amplifying human intelligence with AI will yield positive outcomes for humanity.
items.title: Richard Socher argues AI's true breakthrough is automating scientific discovery rather than chatbots

items.summary: An article notes that the 1953 overthrow of Iranian Prime Minister Mohammad Mossadegh was carried out under CIA direction as an act of U.S. foreign policy. Decades later, President Donald Trump stated it was time for Ukraine to get a new president, claiming Volodymyr Zelenskyy’s attacks on Russian refineries hurt American farmers and ranchers who need diesel. Trump added, “He better damn well stop.”
items.title: Trump Compares 1953 Iran Coup to Ukraine Pressure

items.summary: Axis Bank reported a 38% increase in profit for the second quarter, attributed to loan growth. Net interest income rose 11.8% year-on-year to 15,371 crore. The net interest margin stood at 3.36%, including foreign currency deposit impacts, while excluding them, it was 3.47% compared to 3.46% in the preceding quarter. Total advances grew 23% year-on-year.
items.title: Axis Bank Reports 38% Profit Rise Driven by Loan Growth

items.summary: The Central Bank of India reported a 21% year-on-year profit increase to Rs 1,469 crore in September 2026. Net interest income rose 26% to Rs 4,146 crore, while other income fell 6% to Rs 1,380 crore. Total income grew 15% to Rs 11,737 crore, and the cost-to-income ratio improved to 58.95%.
items.title: Central Bank of India Reports Q2 Profit Jump

items.summary: As anti-gender campaigns and transphobia rise globally, the article examines Michel Foucault's relevance to contemporary culture wars. While U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and former President Trump advocate for binary gender restrictions, the piece highlights Foucault's theoretical foundations for gender studies and queer theory. Philosophers Paul B. Preciado and Rodrigo Castro explain how Foucault analyzed power, exclusion, and the body, arguing that his work offers tools for resistance against domination. New publications of his previously unpublished texts, such as 'The Hermaphrodites,' further explore the distinction between anatomical sex and sexuality, challenging rigid societal categories.
items.title: Foucault's Legacy in the Face of Anti-Gender Backlash

items.summary: A 25-second Al Jazeera video allegedly shows Mexican, Colombian, and Panamanian fighters, including CJNG members, participating in Ukraine's war. This footage has reignited debate regarding the infiltration of organized crime into the conflict. Henry Ziemer of CSIS describes the situation as a 'real recruitment channel' where cartels seek drone expertise and technical modifications. The U.S. government reported 34,682 drone flights near its southern border in fiscal year 2025. In response, authorities in Mexico and the U.S. have invested in signal jammers, though cartels are increasingly adopting fiber-optic drones immune to jamming. A seizure in Mazatlán recovered 15 FPV drones and related equipment, marking the first official record of such technology adapted by Mexican criminal groups.
items.title: Mexican Cartels Adopt Ukrainian Drone Tactics

items.summary: A truck crashed into devotees outside the Sheetla Mata temple in Gwalior on October 18, 2026, killing at least 15 and injuring more than 25. Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister Mohan Yadav ordered police suspensions and a detailed inquiry. Authorities announced compensation for victims and stated that security arrangements will be reviewed to prevent future incidents.
items.title: Truck Crash at Gwalior Temple Kills 15, Triggers Police Action

items.summary: Voxel51 has released version 3.0 of its data platform, designed for teams training models on sensor data from robots, vehicles, and factories. The update introduces Voxel51 Agent, which includes over 45 MCP tools and 80 operators, alongside new time-series support and agentic labeling capabilities. The platform offers a free tier with 30,000 inference requests and 30 compute hours monthly, though it caps datasets at 10,000 samples each. Voxel51 cites its own 2026 survey indicating that exceptional teams spend more than half their project time on data work, compared to 21% of struggling teams. The release also features enhanced data provenance and model-agnostic workflows.
items.title: Voxel51 Launches 3.0 Platform for Physical AI Data

items.summary: The Indian Centre has directed Meta to overhaul its content promotion systems on Facebook and Instagram to prevent disproportionate exposure to limited narratives. The advisory, issued by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology on October 10, requires Meta to strengthen mechanisms for identifying content that could cause public confusion or violence. It also mandates cooperation with law enforcement agencies under the IT Rules, 2021, and the Information Technology Act, 2000.
items.title: India's Centre directs Meta to overhaul content algorithms on Facebook and Instagram

items.summary: Jammu Police questioned the wife of a serving Army officer regarding alleged espionage activities involving Chinese intelligence operatives. Authorities claim she used AI tools like ChatGPT and Claude to prepare sensitive research papers on defense and geopolitical issues. The woman, currently cooperating with investigators, maintains her work relied on open-source material. A forensic examination of her devices is underway.
items.title: Army Officer's Wife Questioned Over AI-Assisted Espionage Allegations

items.summary: Anthropic has granted external evaluators from METR employee-like access to its internal systems to assess AI model risks. This move follows commitments to increase safeguards against catastrophic AI control issues. While critics cite potential conflicts of interest, Anthropic argues that sharing information publicly could benefit malicious actors, comparing its approach to bank supervision where regulators assign resident examiners. OpenAI has yet to outline similar plans.
items.title: Anthropic Grants External Evaluators Employee-Like Access to Assess AI Risks

items.summary: IT firms HCL Technologies and Tech Mahindra surpassed Tata Consultancy Services in net headcount additions during the September-ending quarter. While TCS adopted a constrained approach, HCL and Tech Mahindra reported significant growth. Experts note a sectoral pivot toward productivity and AI, with hiring becoming more selective and project-driven rather than mass-based. Campus recruitment is expected to recover but at a reduced scale compared to previous years.
items.title: HCL and Tech Mahindra Overtake TCS in IT Hiring Adds

items.summary: Amazon has warned it may close warehouses and move thousands of delivery jobs from New York City if the Delivery Protection Act passes. The bill would require Amazon to directly hire 5,000 drivers currently working for contractors. Industry analysts suggest Amazon is likely to follow through, citing a recent decision to shutter facilities in Canada rather than compromise its logistics model. Small business owners fear being wiped out if the legislation is enacted.
items.title: Amazon Warns of Job Losses in NYC Over New Delivery Mandate

items.summary: Ashley St. Clair alleges Elon Musk reduced her child support payments following her public revelation of their son's birth in February 2025. She claims an initial offer of $15 million and $100,000 monthly support was declined, leading to a reduction to $40,000 and then $20,000. These claims appear in a new documentary by Alex Gibney, with no public response from Musk.
items.title: Ashley St. Clair Alleges Elon Musk Reduced Child Support After Public Announcement

items.summary: Analysts expect Infosys to report modest Q2FY27 revenue growth of 1.1–1.7% in constant currency terms. Brokers project revenue between ₹49,090 crore and ₹49,323 crore. Due to demand uncertainties, analysts anticipate a possible cut in FY27 growth guidance, with some expecting a reduction to 1.5–2.5%.
items.title: Analysts Predict Modest Infosys Q2 Revenue Growth and Potential Guidance Cut

items.summary: TikTok permanently suspended Bleecker Street's advertising account for the Elon Musk documentary due to political-content policy violations, according to The Hollywood Reporter. The distributor is appealing the ban as the film expands to over 470 theaters. TikTok cited severe policy breaches, while other platforms like X also rejected ads for the film.
items.title: TikTok Suspends Bleecker Street Ad Account for Musk Documentary

items.summary: Ashley St. Clair alleges Elon Musk reduced her child support payments after she rejected a non-disclosure agreement and publicly revealed her son Romulus' birth in February 2025. St. Clair claims payments dropped from $100,000 to $20,000 monthly. Musk disputes these claims, stating she was never offered the deal and accusing her of making false statements. A custody dispute over Romulus is also ongoing.
items.title: Ashley St. Clair Alleges Elon Musk Cut Child Support

items.summary: Protests in France have highlighted the role of social media in mobilizing demonstrators, particularly through an anonymous TikTok account that posted a video on September 7 calling for street demonstrations on October 17. The video reportedly garnered over 600,000 likes and nearly 10,000 comments, drawing attention from French newspaper Le Monde. While the call for protests on October 17 gained traction, no organization or official page linked to the Yellow Vests appears to be behind it. The movement, reminiscent of the 2018 Yellow Vests protests driven by anger over fuel prices and the cost of living, has seen significant engagement on platforms like TikTok, with videos mentioning the date attracting 132 million cumulative views. On October 17, an estimated 550,000 people participated in marches across France, according to the French interior ministry.
items.title: Anonymous TikTok Account Revives Yellow Vest Protests in France

items.summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent stated that Washington requested European allies to impose secondary tariffs on India and China regarding Russian energy purchases. He noted the refusal and questioned why the US should pressure Moscow while European nations continue buying Russian energy themselves.
items.title: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent Claims Europe Refused Tariffs on India and China

items.summary: Congress MP Bimol Akoijam stated he is willing to contest next year's Manipur Assembly elections from the Keishamthong constituency if the party offers him a ticket. He faces a sexual harassment case and was dismissed from JNU, where he denied the charges as a witch hunt. Delhi Police booked him following complaints from students. Akoijam urged attention to Manipur's crisis while alleging the action against him was to silence his voice.
items.title: Congress MP Akoijam Willing to Contest Manipur Elections Amid Harassment Probe

items.summary: A podcast episode examines whether Europe's regulatory framework is sufficient for advanced AI systems as they become more autonomous. Host Ramsha Jahangir interviews Risto Uuk of the Future of Life Institute and MEP Brando Benifei regarding the debate over liability. The discussion highlights that while the EU AI Act has enforcement powers, it lacks a comprehensive civil liability regime. Benifei argues that the withdrawn AI Liability Directive was a mistake, noting that existing rules make it difficult for victims to prove fault and causation against opaque AI systems. He calls for a renewed legislative approach to establish clear responsibilities among developers, deployers, and operators. The Commission maintains the current framework is adequate, having requested information from over 30 AI firms, but critics argue this is insufficient without stronger enforcement and a dedicated liability structure to prevent market fragmentation.
items.title: Europe Debates Liability Framework for Advanced AI Systems

items.summary: Chinese artists presented the original musical The City of Stars to showcase Xiongan New Area in Hebei Province as an intelligent and futuristic hub. The production utilized advanced machinery and innovative design to recreate the region's three distinct cities on stage. A 2023 premiere featured insights from the cast and crew regarding their artistic interpretation of the area's development.
items.title: Chinese Artists Depict Xiongan's Vision in High-Tech Theater

items.summary: An article describes a new Tesla feature, Automatic Collision Evasion, which autonomously activates Full Self-Driving to avoid collisions. The author, who uses the system, reports a personal incident where the feature swerved to avoid a truck. However, the author notes that access to this feature is restricted to customers paying $99/month for FSD V14 on vehicles with Hardware 4 built since mid-2023. Consequently, approximately 85% of Tesla owners, including millions of customers, reportedly lack access to this safety functionality. The author questions the moral justification for this limitation, contrasting it with the open patenting of seatbelts and noting that Tesla is removing automatic lane assist from non-paying customers.
items.title: Tesla Introduces New Safety Feature Accessible Only to Paying Customers

items.summary: At meetings in Thailand, policy makers and industry leaders gathered to address the dual nature of artificial intelligence. They aim to ensure the technology benefits humanity while preventing it from leaving workers behind, particularly in developing economies. The discussion highlights that AI is already transforming nearly every aspect of the global economy, prompting a focus on managing potential risks alongside opportunities.
items.title: IMF and World Bank Leaders Discuss AI Risks and Benefits in Thailand

items.summary: Parents allege negligence after 23 female students were injured in Hyderabad. While doctors treated 20 students on stretchers at Pratyusha Hospital, parents claim they received no information from college management and learned of the incident from friends. One student died from a severe head injury. Nine others were shifted to other hospitals. Parents demand justice and accountability from the institution.
items.title: Parents allege negligence after 23 female students injured in Hyderabad

items.summary: The nomination process for Andhra Pradesh urban local body elections concluded amid political tensions, with the State Election Commission reviewing complaints. While officials accepted papers from candidates meeting the 3 pm deadline, YSR Congress leaders alleged they were prevented from filing in several areas. Scrutiny is scheduled for October 19, with polling set for October 28. In Guntur, the Telugu Desam party filed nominations successfully.
items.title: Andhra Pradesh Urban Local Body Nominations End Amid Political Tensions

items.summary: Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff escaped unhurt after assailants fired at his car in Mumbai's Juhu area, injuring his driver. The Maharashtra Chief Minister assured safety and ordered a swift investigation, while police deployed forensic units and citywide curfews. Opposition leaders criticized the law and order situation, citing previous attacks on film personalities. Authorities are conducting a manhunt for the attackers.
items.title: Maharashtra CM Assures Safety After Tiger Shroff Targeted in Mumbai Shooting

items.summary: Edimar Martins, a 49-year-old bricklayer from Maranhão, sold his belongings and travelled 1,200 miles (1,931 km) to Belo Horizonte to meet a woman he believed he would marry. He discovered the social media account featuring Jessica Oliveira, which had over 300,000 followers, was fake. The persona, confirmed to be AI-generated, denied interacting with him. Martins, who sought companionship after his mother's death, was left stranded but received assistance from social workers. Despite the disappointment, he plans to return to Belo Horizonte to find another partner.
items.title: Brazilian Man Travels to Meet AI Girlfriend

items.summary: Violent cost-of-living protests across Italy resulted in 28 arrests and 141 injured officers, according to Sky TG24. Clashes occurred in Milan, Turin, Bologna, Brescia, and Bergamo, with organized groups opposing rising living costs. Authorities reported 197 people identified, including 12 minors. Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni expressed solidarity with law enforcement, while local mayors condemned the violence. A retail association estimated shop damage at more than €500,000.
items.title: Violent Cost-of-Living Protests in Italy Result in Arrests and Injuries

items.summary: US Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee condemned a settler attack on Washington Post photojournalist Heidi Levine as a "despicable act of terror" and called for the arrest and prosecution of the perpetrators. Levine, 63, was beaten by masked settlers while Palestinian farmers harvested olives in the West Bank, sustaining injuries requiring surgery. While Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu referred to the assault as "alleged" pending clarification, Levine expressed shock at the ambiguity. Huckabee emphasized that attacking a female journalist was cowardly. Meanwhile, violence against European diplomats visiting the region also surged, prompting calls from the EU and France for accountability. Levine plans to return to work once recovered.
items.title: US Ambassador Denounces Settler Attack on American Photojournalist as Terror

items.summary: Violence has intensified in Iran's Sistan-Baluchistan province, where armed groups clash daily with security forces. Experts note that separatist and Islamist militants are coordinating efforts to challenge the state, potentially exploiting ethnic grievances. The region's strategic importance, including its port Chabahar, heightens concerns as Iran faces pressure from the US and Israel. Recent attacks target the IRGC and police, prompting increased security operations and an execution of a prominent militant. Analysts warn that localized unrest could evolve into a broader security challenge, especially during potential new conflicts.
items.title: Escalating Baluch Insurgency Threatens Iran's Security Amid Regional Tensions

items.summary: US President Donald Trump endorsed Benjamin Netanyahu ahead of Israel's parliamentary election, praising him as a 'great warrior prime minster.' However, the endorsement may not boost Netanyahu's right-wing Likud party, as Israeli public support for Trump has diminished due to disagreements over Iran. Polls suggest no candidate has a clear path to power in the upcoming vote.
items.title: Trump Endorses Netanyahu Amid Israeli Election Uncertainty

items.summary: GP Singh, the CRPF director general, commended a female officer for displaying patience and resilience after being slapped by a protester during a CJP march in Delhi. Delhi Police filed an FIR against the unidentified woman for assaulting the officer and violating prohibitory orders. The incident occurred near Connaught Place on Friday evening, and authorities are identifying the woman for legal action.
items.title: CRPF Chief Commends Officer for Resilience After Protester Assault

items.summary: President Trump waived sanctions on Russia under the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act, a move supported by cabinet members Marco Rubio and Scott Bessent. While the US requested European allies impose secondary sanctions on China and India for purchasing Russian oil, they refused. Critics, including Senator Darline Graham and lawmakers, condemned the decision as undermining Congress and aiding Putin.
items.title: Trump Waives Sanctions on Russia Despite European Refusal to Target China and India

items.summary: Five years after announcing an ambitious privatisation programme, the Indian government faces criticism for limited sales of Air India, Neelachal Ispat, and IDBI Bank. Critics argue the policy remains a failure as the state continues collecting dividends and leasing assets. The recent IDBI sale to Fairfax Financial Holdings, approved below the initial reserve price, highlights unresolved issues regarding valuation methods and potential conflicts of interest involving LIC and Fairfax's insurer.
items.title: Government Criticized for Ineffective Disinvestment Strategy Over Five Years

items.summary: A senior journalist argues that labeling current pro-democracy demonstrators as anti-national is historically inconsistent, citing the violent nature of the 1973-74 Navnirman agitation in Gujarat and Bihar. The article highlights that key figures in the ruling BJP, including then-Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Morarji Desai, and George Fernandes, made provocative statements and advocated for extra-constitutional means or strikes to remove Prime Minister Indira Gandhi during that period. The writer contends that these past actions by now-celebrated leaders were not considered anti-national, questioning why current peaceful protesters are treated differently despite posing no threat to public order.
items.title: Article Argues Agitation Is Not Anti-National In India

items.summary: Volodymyr Zelenskyy thanked the Trump administration for resuming intelligence sharing regarding Russian ballistic missile strikes but accused the US of intentionally throttling Starlink speeds to send a message. Zelenskyy stated SpaceX executed the speed limits, while Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent denied the administration ordered the action, calling Zelenskyy's claims reckless. Amidst ongoing strikes on Ukraine's energy infrastructure, Zelenskyy criticized Trump's push for a ceasefire and sanctions relief, arguing Russia continues aggressive attacks without reciprocal steps. Tensions remain high as Ukraine resumes strikes on Russian oil facilities and drones occasionally enter NATO airspace, raising fears of conflict spillover.
items.title: Zelenskyy Credits Trump for Intelligence Sharing but Accuses US of Starlink Throttling

items.summary: Marine Le Pen, the far-right candidate for the 2027 French presidential election, declared a crisis of confidence and a threat to democracy following renewed looting in Paris. She blamed the far left and President Emmanuel Macron, whom she described as lacking credibility. Meanwhile, Jordan Bardella stated that order no longer exists in France. Authorities reported over 30,000 looters in Marseille on Saturday alone.
items.title: Marine Le Pen Warns of Democracy Threat Amid Paris Riots

items.summary: Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis and Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde condemned a shooting incident targeting actor Tiger Shroff in Mumbai's Juhu area. Fadnavis confirmed speaking to the actor and police commissioner, urging swift action to apprehend the assailants. Shinde stated that police teams have been formed to identify and arrest those responsible, warning that no gang would be spared. Other leaders, including NCP President Supriya Sule and Union Minister Piyush Goyal, also expressed concern over the incident and the state's law and order situation. Preliminary reports indicate three unidentified men on a motorcycle opened fire, injuring three individuals, including the actor's driver.
items.title: Maharashtra Leaders Condemn Shooting of Actor Tiger Shroff in Mumbai

items.summary: Edward Cutler reviews a book titled *This Beautiful Country*, subtitled *How Italy’s Nature Shaped its Culture and Civilisation*. Cutler describes the book as excellent for explaining how Italy's natural environment, including mountains and rivers, has influenced its culture. The review highlights Italy as a botanical crossroads hosting at least 140 native tree species, noting unique varieties like the Sicilian fir and Etna birch. Cutler recommends the book to those interested in Italy.
items.title: Edward Cutler Reviews Book on Italy's Nature Shaping Culture

items.summary: Following Character.AI's bankruptcy filing, Disney agreed to hire at least 60 employees, representing the majority of the workforce, with an estimated $60 million in annual compensation. The deal, described as a stalking horse bid, allows other companies to submit higher offers. Disney CEO Karandeep Anand previously became the company's first CTO. The agreement stems from a $20 million asset acquisition deal. Character.AI faces regulatory scrutiny and litigation, including a lawsuit involving a child safety incident.
items.title: Disney to Hire Majority of Bankrupt Character.AI Workforce

items.summary: Noah Adams, a longtime host of NPR's All Things Considered, has died at age 84. His wife, Neenah Ellis, confirmed the news. Colleagues remember Adams for his deep curiosity and ability to connect with people, often avoiding official sources in favor of genuine stories. He worked in rural America and produced experimental documentaries. His style influenced colleagues like Ira Glass and Susan Stamberg, who praised his quiet confidence and observational skills. Adams wrote five books and shaped NPR's identity during its formative years.
items.title: Noah Adams, NPR Host and Storyteller, Dies at 84

items.summary: Jason Miller, an assistant lecturer at North Carolina State University, argues that poet Langston Hughes significantly influenced singer Nina Simone's career. Miller documents their friendship starting in 1949, noting Hughes encouraged Simone to record
items.title: Scholar Reveals Langston Hughes Encouraged Nina Simone's Career

items.summary: Barcelona coach Hansi Flick faces a significant setback ahead of a crucial week. The club confirmed injuries to defenders Jules Kounde and Eric Garcia on social media. Garcia is ruled out for three to four weeks with a thigh injury, while Kounde will miss the PSG game but may return against Real Madrid. Additionally, Gerard Martin exited Saturday's 5-2 win over Real Betis at halftime, and Andreas Christensen remains injured, limiting options for the upcoming matches.
items.title: Barcelona Coach Hansi Flick Faces Injury Crisis Ahead of PSG and Real Madrid Matches

items.summary: Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar stated that recent violent riots in France justified his government's strict migration policies. While Macron and Sánchez defended immigrants, Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk also emphasized maintaining strict asylum rules. Magyar's comments drew criticism from Hungarian activists who accused him of exploiting the unrest for political gain, noting that most protesters were French nationals.
items.title: Hungarian PM Links French Riots to Migration Amid European Debate

items.summary: Violent protests and looting occurred in Paris, Lyon, and Marseille following nationwide demonstrations against the rising cost of living. In Lyon, firefighters extinguished a blaze at the city's tourist office, while nearby shops were vandalized. Paris saw shattered windows at the Les Halles shopping centre and the Paris Opera. In Marseille, crews cleaned debris from Rue Saint-Ferréol. Municipal workers, shopkeepers, and volunteers are now clearing broken glass and repairing storefronts across the three cities.
items.title: Paris, Lyon and Marseille Assess Damage Following Violent Protests

items.summary: Parents of IIT-Bombay student Sahil Wakode were detained by Mumbai Police while protesting his suicide death. Student groups accused police of excessive force. The institute claimed Wakode cheated on an exam, while his father alleged caste discrimination. Police registered a case against a professor for abetment to suicide. Both sides remain at odds regarding the cause of the tragedy.
items.title: Parents of IIT-B Student Detained During Campus Protest Over Suicide

items.summary: An overnight attack on St Petersburg killed at least one person and injured five, targeting oil facilities, a logistics centre, and data centres. Governor Alexander Beglov reported fires being extinguished at the St Petersburg Oil Terminal and Ruchyi oil depot. Ukraine resumed strikes on Russian energy infrastructure after a pause, while Kyiv has not yet commented on the specific strikes. Russia claims to have shot down over 1,000 drones overnight.
items.title: Overnight Attack Hits Oil Facilities in St Petersburg

items.summary: Two gangsters linked to the Lawrence Bishnoi gang claimed responsibility for an attack on Tiger Shroff's BMW in Mumbai. News agency ANI reported that the actor escaped unhurt after three to four rounds were allegedly fired at his vehicle while he was leaving a ground.
items.title: Lawrence Bishnoi Gang Claims Responsibility for Attack on Tiger Shroff's Car

items.summary: Pacific General Electric (PGE) promotes electric medium- and heavy-duty trucks as valuable grid support, calling them 'batteries on wheels.' During an Oregon event, PGE manager Karla Hendrickson dismissed claims that electric vehicles overload the grid. She noted these trucks can help manage high demand while keeping costs low. Gerick Kransky of the Oregon Department of Environmental Quality added that while these vehicles are few, they cause disproportionate emissions.
items.title: PGE Highlights Electric Trucks as Grid Backup Assets

items.summary: Eight MGNREGA workers were killed and 12 injured when a speeding car struck them near Alisher village in Sangrur district, Punjab, police said. The incident occurred on Sunday as workers were engaged in tasks near the road. The driver abandoned the vehicle and fled. Officials have deployed ambulances and are providing medical aid to the victims while expressing grief over the tragedy.
items.title: Eight MGNREGA Workers Killed in Sangrur Road Accident

items.summary: Automakers are developing faster and smarter electric vehicles to overcome consumer stigma and rising fuel costs. High-end electric supercars now offer rapid acceleration and advanced technology, while extended-range electric vehicles are being introduced for trucks and SUVs in markets like the United States. Specific models, such as the Jeep Grand Wagoneer REEV and the Stellantis RAM 1500 REV, are expected to launch in late 2026 with significant electric range and total range capabilities. Luxury brands like Jaguar and Bentley are also unveiling new electric models with competitive pricing and performance features. However, questions remain about whether high-end vehicle drivers will fully switch to electric options.
items.title: Automakers Push Electric Supercars and Trucks with New Range and Speed

items.summary: Abhishek Bisen, Head of Fixed Income at Kotak Mahindra Asset Management Company, states that bond yields touching 8 per cent on longer-dated government and quasi-government bonds represent a historical sweet spot for long-term investors. He attributes the surge in yields to central bank rate hikes, geopolitical conflicts in West Asia, and rising US Treasury yields. While acknowledging that equity markets have corrected and offer long-term value, Bisen advises against pausing equity SIPs entirely, suggesting instead a balanced approach with a debt allocation of around 20 to 30 per cent. He notes that while duration assets create significant volatility, capital loss is exceptionally rare in India for high-quality sovereign or corporate bonds held over 18 months. Bisen recommends utilizing SIPs or staggered allocations rather than trying to time the market perfectly.
items.title: Bond yields at 8 pc offer sweet spot for debt investors: Abhishek Bisen

items.summary: Eight MGNREGA workers died after a speeding car hit them near Alisher village in Sangrur, Punjab. Harvinder Singh, a nearby factory worker, rescued the victims and alleged administrative negligence, noting the ambulance took nearly an hour to arrive. Five died on the spot while three succumbed later. Another witness claimed authorities delayed arrival to complete formalities. The driver, Pargat Singh Kala, escaped the scene.
items.title: Eight Labourers Killed in Sangrur After Speeding Car Accident

items.summary: Pope Leo XIV appeared in St. Peter's Square to thank the faithful for their prayers following surgery to remove a malignant tumor from his lung. The 71-year-old pontiff, who has held office for 17 months, stated he plans to gradually resume his duties with God's help. He expressed gratitude to medical staff at Gemelli Hospital and noted the experience brought him closer to those facing illness. Histological testing is underway to determine if additional treatment is needed.
items.title: Pope Leo XIV Returns to Public After Lung Surgery

items.summary: EcoFlow has introduced the Titan 5000, a modular residential battery system starting at 5 kWh and scalable up to 30 kWh. The entry model offers 4 kW output, while higher tiers reach 7.2 kW continuous or 10 kW peak power with solar integration. Brian Essenmacher, Head of US Business Development at EcoFlow, stated the system provides a practical way for families to manage energy intelligently. Pre-orders require a $50 payment with savings available upon release.
items.title: EcoFlow Launches Scalable Residential Battery System Titan 5000

items.summary: An investigation is underway into a £55m loan provided to Manchester City's Abu Dhabi owner while Andy Burnham served as mayor. Councillors plan to review loans made to property companies during his tenure. The loans funded the Manchester Life housing development, which aimed to create 6,000 homes. GMCA states the fund has built 11,000 homes and lent to 50 developers, though the specific interest rate and eligibility criteria for the Sheikh Mansour loan remain undisclosed.
items.title: Investigation launched into £55m housing loan to Manchester City owner

items.summary: French police arrested approximately 1,800 people following violent protests and widespread looting across France. Interior Minister Laurent Nunez confirmed the arrests and stated that investigations are underway to identify perpetrators. President Emmanuel Macron is expected to address the nation regarding the unrest, which has caused significant damage to businesses and public property. While the interior ministry reported 550,000 attendees at the nationwide demonstrations, the CGT union claimed 800,000 participants. The violence, described by officials as unprecedented in Paris, has led to injuries among police and emergency personnel, as well as the death of one individual unrelated to the protests.
items.title: French Police Arrest 1,800 Amid Violent Protests and Looting

items.summary: Hackers are exploiting an OS command-injection vulnerability in SiteGuard Server Edition, allowing execution of commands with root or SYSTEM privileges. The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-106931, affects the statistics feature in host-based WAF instances. SiteGuard, a Japanese vendor protecting over 1.5 million websites, has issued a bulletin confirming abuse. The vendor advises administrators to preserve evidence before patching, as remediation may erase attack traces.
items.title: Hackers Exploit SiteGuard WAF Flaw for Admin Access

items.summary: Richard Cooke, a humanities scholar, wrote a book about the human history of Wikipedia to understand why the platform works despite its reputation. He highlights the founders' philosophical backgrounds and the community's unique culture, noting its incompleteness and the central role of neurodiversity. Cooke argues that while Wikipedia is massive and widely used, it faces existential threats from AI encroachment and declining web traffic. He believes the platform will survive, but its foundations are quaking, making its current state urgent to document before it changes forever. The book, titled 'The Last Best Place on the Internet', is set for release in November.
items.title: Richard Cooke explores the human history and future fragility of Wikipedia

items.summary: Victorian Coalition MPs criticized Advance's pre-election campaign as bizarre, warning it could jeopardize their majority government status. Advance dismissed the criticism, claiming the Coalition is not polling well. The group plans to run ads in 20 seats, including those held by Labor and contested by One Nation. Advance argues that without preferences, Labor cannot win alone, while Coalition sources claim the campaign undermines their message.
items.title: Victorian Coalition Warns Advance Campaign May Cost Majority

items.summary: A search for Amelia Earhart's plane wreckage on Nikumaroro Island has resumed after severe weather halted researchers for three days. The team, led by Purdue University and the Archaeological Legacy Institute, aims to investigate the Taraia Object spotted in aerial imagery. While the expedition was delayed by strong winds and El Niño conditions, researchers hope to complete their underwater survey. The search continues to explore theories that Earhart may have ditched her plane near the island, though skepticism remains regarding the Taraia Object's identity.
items.title: Search for Amelia Earhart's plane resumes after stormy weather

items.summary: Gabon is implementing strict measures to protect the sacred iboga plant from commercial exploitation by US pharmaceutical companies seeking to use it for addiction treatment. While US interest has surged following an executive order and a study showing potential benefits for veterans, Gabonese authorities warn of ecological threats from over-harvesting. In response, the government has recognized traditional knowledge as national heritage and adopted a draft decree prohibiting the export of iboga and its derivatives. Leaders argue that protecting the plant and its associated culture is essential to prevent the resource from being stripped of its value while the country receives little benefit.
items.title: Gabon Bans Iboga Export to Protect Sacred Plant from US Pharmaceutical Demand

items.summary: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) issued a fresh advisory on October 15 requiring food businesses to maintain controlled temperatures during the storage and transport of perishable items like paneer, meat, and fish. The directive, issued under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, emphasizes hygiene, proper packaging, and suitable vehicles to prevent contamination and spoilage. Non-compliance may result in seizure of food items and destruction by authorities.
items.title: FSSAI Issues Fresh Advisory on Perishable Food Storage and Transport

items.summary: Alberta and Québec are considering independence referendums, with polls indicating 70 per cent of residents in both provinces favour remaining in Canada. While Alberta’s Premier Danielle Smith announced a vote to unite her party, Québec’s Parti Québecois leader Paul St-Pierre Plamondon delayed a planned 2028 referendum until after Donald Trump leaves office. Trump’s threats of annexation and tariffs loom large, affecting the provinces differently; Québec’s economy has been hit harder by tariffs on manufacturing and aluminum. Despite these challenges, Smith rejects postponing the vote, while Plamondon seeks to protect French culture and autonomy. Both leaders face internal political risks if their respective referendums fail or succeed.
items.title: Alberta and Québec Referendums Test Canadian Unity Amid U.S. Hostility

items.summary: Leigh Hoffman won silver in the men's individual sprint at the UCI track world championships in Shanghai, finishing behind Dutch rider Harrie Lavreysen. Hoffman, who previously won bronze, expressed satisfaction despite the narrow loss. Australia secured two medals total, down from five the previous year, while Lavreysen extended his record to 23 world titles.
items.title: Australia Claims Second Silver at Track Cycling World Championships

items.summary: This article outlines a ten-step process for passengers seeking refunds and compensation from airlines under U.S. Department of Transportation and EU261 regulations. It explains that entitlement depends on whether the disruption was within the carrier's control and details specific rules for cancellations, significant schedule changes, and denied boarding. The guide emphasizes that refunds are not automatic and often require written requests, while EU261 provides fixed cash compensation for qualifying delays. It also covers procedures for filing DOT complaints, pursuing credit card chargebacks, and using small claims court as a final resort. The text advises passengers to document delays immediately and distinguish between controllable and uncontrollable causes to maximize their chances of success.
items.title: A guide to claiming airline refunds and compensation under U.S. and EU rules

items.summary: The article outlines practical strategies for travelers to secure better airline seats without paying additional fees or holding elite status. It explains that while airlines have unbundled pricing, gaps remain in seat availability due to system behaviors like last-minute inventory releases, aircraft swaps, and check-in timing. Tactics include checking in immediately when the window opens, using airline seat maps before booking, joining free loyalty programs, and asking gate agents about unassigned seats. The text notes that these methods apply across major U.S. carriers like Delta, American, and United, though specifics vary by fare class and route. It also warns that basic economy tickets often restrict seat selection, making timing and flexibility crucial for finding open seats.
items.title: Strategies for Securing Better Airline Seats Without Extra Costs

items.summary: Seventeen-year-old Scottish judoka Lexi Buchanan traveled to Japan alone to address a lack of female sparring partners in Scotland. Buchanan noted that while she competes at 48 kilos, the next female competitors are around 63 kilos and upwards. She arrived without corporate sponsors or a national team delegation for a self-driven, three-month mission to improve her development.
items.title: Scottish Teen Lexi Buchanan Trains Alone in Japan to Find Female Sparring Partners

items.summary: Experts remain divided on whether the Milwaukee Brewers' National League Championship Series sweep of the Los Angeles Dodgers will influence Major League Baseball labor negotiations. While owners push for a salary cap opposed by players, the Brewers' victory, which marks their first World Series appearance in 44 years, weakens the owners' argument regarding a lack of parity in the sport, according to labor lawyer Tony Torain.
items.title: Experts Divided on Brewers' Sweep Impact on MLB Labor Talks

items.summary: The Delhi government released a draft scheme capping the e-rickshaw fleet at 250,000 vehicles to address traffic congestion, road safety, and pollution. Open for public consultation until 30 days, the policy restricts residents to five vehicles and mandates digital compliance certificates. Officials attribute current traffic issues to the unregulated proliferation of these three-wheelers.
items.title: Delhi Government Proposes Cap on E-Rickshaw Fleet to Address Traffic and Pollution

items.summary: Iran's parliament approved Mehrdad Akhlaghi Ketabchi as defence minister. He warned Washington and allies would suffer "enormous damage" if military operations resume. Akhlaghi, 68, brings decades of missile expertise and faces US sanctions. The appointment follows the killing of his predecessor during US-Israeli strikes. President Trump indicated no attack before the 3rd November elections, though tensions remain high.
items.title: New Iranian Defence Minister Warns US of Enormous Damage If Military Campaign Resumes

items.summary: An estimated 550,000 people participated in protests across France demanding investment in education and action on the cost of living. The demonstrations quickly descended into violence with cars and buildings set alight. At least 1,200 people were arrested as riot police deployed tear gas and water cannons. French President Emmanuel Macron denounced the violence and promised prosecution for vandals.
items.title: Disorder Erupts During Massive Protests Across France

items.summary: Meta updated its commercial terms of use to allow content use for AI training, sparking concerns among legal experts and publishers. While Meta previously faced a copyright lawsuit, a spokesperson clarified that the updated terms only applied to ads and business products. Meta stated the change did not alter how web crawlers function and removed the specific provision following public feedback.
items.title: Meta Removes Controversial Scraping and AI Training Language from Terms
